Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 1:

The interpretation of His words, may His majesty and the sanctity of His names be exalted: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [25:1].

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: "Tabaraka" (blessed, exalted): it is of the form tafa'ala, derived from "barakah" (blessing).

As related:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Umarah narrated to us, saying: Abu Rawq narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: "Tabaraka" is of the form tafa'ala, from "barakah." It is like the saying of one who says: "Tuqaddasa Rabbuna" (our Lord is sanctified). So His words ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion﴾ mean: Blessed is He who sent down the distinction between truth and falsehood, detail after detail and surah after surah, upon His servant Muhammad (ﷺ), so that Muhammad would be a caller to Him for all of the jinn and mankind to whom Allah sent him, a warner: meaning, one who warns them of His punishment and frightens them with His torment, if they do not affirm His oneness and do not devote worship sincerely to Him, and renounce everything else worshipped besides Him, of deities and idols.

And it is in line with what we have said that the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾: "[The warner is] the Prophet, the warner." He recited ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [35:24], and recited ﴿And We did not destroy any town but that it had warners﴾ [26:208], and said: "The warners are the messengers." He said: "Dhul-Qarnayn was a single warner who reached between the east and the west, then reached the two barriers, and he was a warner, though I have not heard anyone affirm that he was a prophet." [He recited] ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [6:19], and said: "Whoever the Qur'an reaches among creation, the Messenger of Allah is their warner." He recited ﴿O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [7:158], and said: "Allah did not send a messenger to people in general except Noah, with whom He began creation, so he was the messenger of all the people of the earth, and Muhammad (ﷺ) was sealed with him."

The commentary on His words, exalted is He: ﴿Him to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in the dominion, and who created everything and determined it with precise measure﴾ (25:2).

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be blessed: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion (al-Furqan), ﴿Him to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. So "alladhi" (who) the second is a qualifier (na't) of "alladhi" the first, and both are in the nominative position: the first by His saying "blessed," and the second is a qualifier of it. By His saying ﴿Him to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ He means: the One who has authority over the heavens and the earth, whose command and decree take effect throughout all of them, and whose rulings proceed over all of them. He says: therefore it is incumbent upon whoever is like this that the people of His dominion and those under His authority obey Him and do not disobey Him. He says: so do not disobey My warner to you, O people, follow him, and act upon the truth that has come to you. ﴿And who has not taken a son﴾: He says, as a refutation of those who attributed a son to Him and said: the angels are daughters of God. He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant has not taken a son, and whoever attributes a son to Him has lied and fabricated against his Lord. ﴿And who has no partner in the dominion﴾: He says, as a refutation of those among the polytheist Arabs who attributed divinity to idols and worshipped them besides God, and who said in their talbiyah: "Here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, whom You possess and who is under Your possession." Those who uttered this statement lied; God has no partner in His dominion and authority such that it would be fitting to worship anyone besides Him. He says, may His remembrance be blessed: so single out, O people, your Lord, who sent down the Criterion upon His servant Muhammad, His prophet (ﷺ), for divinity, and devote worship to Him alone, apart from all that you worship besides Him, of gods, idols, angels, jinn, and humans, for all of that is His creation and within His dominion. Worship is therefore fitting only for God, who is the owner of all of that. As for His saying ﴿and who created everything﴾: He says, may His remembrance be blessed: and He who sent down the Criterion upon Muhammad created everything; all things are His creation and His possession, and slaves owe obedience to their owner and service to their master, to none other. He says: I am your Creator and your Owner, so devote worship to Me alone, apart from others. As for His saying ﴿and determined it with precise measure﴾: He says: He arranged everything He created and made it fit for what suits it, so there is no defect in it and no disparity.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 3:

The discussion of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods who create nothing while they are themselves created, and who possess no power to harm or benefit even themselves, and possess no power over death or life or resurrection﴾ (25:3).

Allah the Exalted says, rebuking the polytheists of the Arabs for their worship of what is other than Him among the gods, and marvelling at those of them who possess intellect, and alerting them to the point of error in their action and their departure from the path of truth, and their riding upon the ways of misguidance, which none rides except one whose judgement is corrupted and whose intellect is deprived: "And these polytheists have taken, besides Him, who possesses the dominion of the heavens and the earth alone, without any partner, who created everything and determined it precisely, gods," meaning idols in their hands which they worship, "that create nothing while they themselves are created, and that possess no power to bring to themselves any benefit they might draw towards themselves, nor any harm they might repel from themselves from one who intends them harm, nor any power to cause a living thing to die, nor to bring a dead thing to life, nor to raise it up again after its death." They abandoned the worship of the Creator of everything, the Creator of their gods, the Owner of harm and benefit, and He in whose hand are death, life and resurrection. And "resurrection" (nushur) is the verbal noun of "nushira al-mayyit nushuran," which means that he is raised up and lives again after death.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "This is not but a fabrication which he has invented, and other people have helped him at it. So they have certainly committed an injustice and a falsehood."﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: those disbelievers in Allah, who took other gods besides Him, said: "What is this Qur'an which Muhammad has brought us?" ﴿Is not but a fabrication﴾, meaning: nothing but lies and slander. ﴿He has invented it﴾, meaning: he fabricated it and concocted it with his words. ﴿And other people have helped him at it﴾. It is related that they used to say: "It is only the Jews who teach Muhammad this which he brings us." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And other people have helped him at it﴾, that is: "And the Jews helped Muhammad in this fabrication which he invented."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿And other people have helped him at it﴾, he said: "The Jews."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So they have certainly committed an injustice and a falsehood﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: those who uttered this saying, namely those who said: ﴿This is not but a fabrication which he has invented, and other people have helped him at it﴾, have committed an injustice, meaning by the injustice their attributing the speech of Allah and His revelation to being a fabrication invented by Muhammad (ﷺ). We have already explained earlier that the meaning of injustice (zulm) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. So the injustice of those who uttered this saying toward the Qur'an, by their statement, was their describing it with other than its attributes. As for zur (falsehood), its root meaning is embellishing falsehood. So the interpretation of the speech is: these people, in their saying ﴿This is not but a fabrication which he has invented, and other people have helped him at it﴾, have come with pure lying.

Those of the people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid; and al-Qasim related to me, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿So they have certainly committed an injustice and a falsehood﴾, he said: "A lie."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verses 5–6:

Interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Legends of the former peoples, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ ﴿Say, "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."﴾

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and that he is the one meant by His words: ﴿And they say, "Legends of the former peoples."﴾

Those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: a shaykh from the people of Egypt, who had arrived some forty-odd years earlier, narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah ibn Alqamah ibn Abd Manaf ibn Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy was among the devils of Quraysh. He used to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and act hostilely toward him. He had traveled to al-Hirah, where he learned the tales of the kings of Persia and the stories of Rustam and Isfandiyar. Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat in a gathering, reminded people of Allah, and recounted to his people what punishments of Allah had befallen the nations before them, al-Nadr would follow him into the gathering after he rose and say: "By Allah, O assembly of Quraysh, I have a better story than his. Come, and I will tell you a better account than his." Then he would relate to them the stories of the kings of Persia, Rustam, and Isfandiyar, and then say: "Muhammad's stories are no better than mine." Thereupon Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed eight verses of the Qur'an concerning al-Nadr, beginning with His words: ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."﴾ And everything in the Qur'an that mentions "legends" (asatir) refers to this.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us... [chain continues with Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Sa'id or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, similarly, except that he stated the words "Allah revealed eight verses concerning al-Nadr" on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas.]

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning ﴿Legends of the former peoples﴾: their poetry and their soothsaying, which al-Nadr ibn al-Harith would say.

The meaning of the statement: The polytheists who said of this Qur'an, ﴿It is nothing but a fabrication he has invented﴾ (about Muhammad (ﷺ)), said: what Muhammad has brought us is "legends of the former peoples," meaning their tales which they used to write down in their books; Muhammad (ﷺ) had them written down from the Jews. ﴿So they are dictated to him﴾ — by this phrase they mean: these legends are read out to him, from their saying "amlaytu 'alayka al-kitab" and "amlaltu" (I dictated the book to you). ﴿Morning and evening﴾ — he says: they are dictated to him at dawn and at dusk.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Say, "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth"﴾

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers of Allah's signs from among your people, the polytheists: the matter is not as you claim, that this Qur'an is the legends of the former peoples, and that Muhammad (ﷺ) invented it and was helped in it by other people. Rather, it is the truth, sent down by the Lord who knows the secret of whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, nothing is hidden from Him, and He takes account of that for His creation and recompenses them for what their hearts have resolved upon and concealed in their souls. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — meaning: He has never ceased pardoning His creation and showing them mercy, bestowing His favor upon them through His forgiveness. He says: since that is His custom with His creation, He gives you respite, O you who utter what you have said of falsehood and who commit the disbelief you have committed.

Those of the exegetes said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning ﴿Say, "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth"﴾: he said, "What the people of the earth and the people of the heavens keep secret."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verses 7–8:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why has an angel not been sent down to him so that he might be a warner with him? Or a treasure be thrown down to him, or he have a garden from which he eats?" And the wrongdoers say, "You are only following a man affected by magic."﴾

It is mentioned that these two verses were revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the polytheists of his people said to him on the night their nobles gathered behind the Ka'bah, and they proposed things to him and asked him for signs.

Among what they said to him at that time, [it was] that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the freedman of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah the freedman of Ibn Abbas, from Ibn Abbas, that they said to him: "If you will not do this for us"—meaning what they asked him of removing our mountains from us, reviving our forefathers, and bringing Allah and the angels as a tribe, and what Allah mentioned in Surat Bani Isra'il—"then take for yourself. Ask your Lord to send an angel with you to affirm what you say and to answer us on your behalf. And ask Him to make for you palaces and gardens and treasures of gold and silver, which will suffice you from what we see you seeking. For you walk in the markets and seek livelihood as we seek it, so that we may know your merit and your station with your Lord, if you are a messenger as you claim." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not do that." So Allah revealed concerning their words, "Take for yourself": what they asked—that He should take for him gardens, palaces and treasures, or send with him an angel to affirm what he says and to repel from him whoever disputes with him. ﴿And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why has an angel not been sent down to him?...﴾

So the meaning of the statement: The polytheists said, "What is with this messenger"—meaning Muhammad (ﷺ)—"who claims that Allah has sent him to us, that he eats food as we eat, and walks in our markets as we walk?" ﴿Why has it not been sent down to him﴾ means: he says, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him from heaven, if he is truthful, so that he would be a warner to the people along with him, affirming what he says? Or a treasure of silver or gold be thrown down to him, so that he would not need to exert himself in seeking livelihood?" ﴿Or he have a garden﴾ means: he says, "Or he have an orchard" ﴿from which he eats﴾.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿yakulu﴾ with the *ya*, meaning: the Messenger eats from it. The majority of the Kufan readers recited ﴿na'kulu minha﴾ with the *nun*, meaning: we eat from the garden.

The more correct of the two recitations in my view is the one who recites it with the *ya*, due to the report we mentioned earlier, that the request of the polytheists to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was that he should ask his Lord for these qualities for himself, not for them. Since their request to him was thus, it is not permissible for them to say to him, "Ask for yourself that, so that we may eat."

Moreover, in the words of His, the Exalted's: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ there is clear evidence that they only said to him, "Request that for yourself, so that you yourself may eat from it, not we."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And the wrongdoers say﴾

It means: the polytheists said to the believers in Allah and His Messenger: ﴿You are only following﴾ O people, by following Muhammad ﴿a man﴾ upon whom there is ﴿magic﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verses 9–10:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Look how they coin comparisons for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾ (9) ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾ (10)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Look, O Muhammad, at these polytheists who have made likenesses for you by their saying about you, "He is bewitched." Thereby they have strayed from the straight path and have gone wrong in the way of guidance and right direction, so they cannot find a way ﴿لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ meaning: they do not find a way to the truth except in what you were sent with, and from the direction in which they went astray.

The exegetes have said what is similar to what we have said in the interpretation of this.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Look how they coin comparisons for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾: that is, they sought guidance in other than what you were sent with to them, so they went astray, and they will never be able to attain guidance in anything other than it.

Others said something else about this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿so they cannot find a way﴾: he said, "A way out that would take them out of the comparisons they coined for you."

* *

His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: may He who, if He wills, will give you better than that be sanctified.

The exegetes differed concerning the referent of "that" in His saying ﴿will give you better than that﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of "that" is: better than what these polytheists said to you, O Muhammad, "Why was he not given this, when he is the Messenger of God?" Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verses 11–12:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Nay, but they denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing Fire. When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring.﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These polytheists did not deny God and reject what you, O Muhammad, brought of the truth because you eat food and walk in the markets; rather, they denied the Hereafter and did not believe in reward and punishment, denying the Resurrection and that God would resurrect the dead to be gathered for the Resurrection.

﴿And We have prepared﴾ means: We have readied for those who deny that God will resurrect the dead alive after their perishing for the establishment of the Hour a fire that is kindled and blazes over them. ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾ means: when this fire which We have prepared for these deniers sees their persons from a distant place, it rages against them, meaning it boils and seethes. It is said: "So-and-so raged (taghayyaza) at so-and-so," meaning he became angry with him, so his chest boiled with anger against him, and it became evident in his speech. ﴿And roaring (zafiran)﴾ means its sound.

If someone says: How is it said ﴿they will hear its raging (taghayyuzan)﴾ when raging cannot be heard? It is said that the meaning is: they will hear the sound of the raging, which is the blazing and kindling.

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mahmud ibn Khidash told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti told us, saying: Asbagh ibn Zayd al-Warraq told us, from Khalid ibn Kathir, from Fudayk, from a man of the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever speaks on my behalf what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire of Hell." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, does it have an eye?" He said: "Have you not heard the words of Allah: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾..." and the verse.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us concerning His saying: ﴿they will hear its raging and roaring﴾, he said: Al-Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir informed me, from Mujahid, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Indeed Hell will emit a roar such that no angel or prophet remains except that he falls down trembling in his knees, until Abraham kneels on his knees and says: "O Lord, today I ask of You only for myself!"

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa told us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Indeed a man will be dragged toward the Fire, and it will shrink and draw its parts together, and the Merciful will say to it: "What is wrong with you?" It will say: "He is seeking refuge from me!" He will say: "Release My servant." And a man will be dragged to the Fire and say: "O Lord, was this the opinion you had of Me?" He will say: "What was your opinion?" He will say: "That Your mercy would encompass me." He said: Then He will say: "Release My servant." And a man will be dragged to the Fire, and the Fire will gasp toward him like a mule's gasp toward barley, and it will emit a roar such that no one remains except that he fears.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 13–14:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein, bound together, they will call out there for destruction.﴾ ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And when these deniers of the Hour are thrown from the Fire into a narrow place, their hands bound to their necks in shackles, ﴿they will call out there for destruction.﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of "thubur" (destruction). Some of them said: it is "woe" (wayl).

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿and call out for many destructions﴾, he said: "woe" (wayl).

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction﴾, he said: Do not call out today for one woe, and call out for many woes.

Others said: "thubur" means ruin (al-halak).

Mention of those who said that:

- I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction﴾: "thubur" is ruin.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: In the speech of the Arabs, the root of "thubur" is a man turning away from something. It is said from it: "What turned you (tharaka) away from this matter?", meaning, what diverted you from it. In this place it is a call of these people with regret over their turning away from obeying God in the world and from believing in what the Prophet of God (ﷺ) brought them, so that they deserved punishment from Him, just as the speaker says: "Woe, my regret! Woe, my sorrow over what I neglected in God's side!" Some of the knowledgeable people of Arabic speech from the people of Basra used to say regarding His words ﴿they will call out there for destruction﴾: it means ruin (halaka), and he would say: it is a verbal noun from "thabara al-rajul," meaning he was destroyed. He cites in support of his view the verse of Ibn al-Zaba'ra:

"When I contend with Satan in the paths of error, and whoever follows his inclination is made a thabur (one destroyed)."

[[The verse is by Abd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra, the poet of Quraysh who used to satirize the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions; then he went out to him and embraced Islam after the conquest of Mecca, and when he embraced Islam he composed poetry, of which this verse is part of a four-verse piece recited by Ibn Ishaq in the Sirah (Halabi edition 4: 61). "Ujari" means: I compete with and oppose. "Sunan" with a vowel is: the middle of the road. "Mathbur" means: destroyed. The evidence in it, according to the author, is that "thubur" means ruin, and "mathbur" means the one ruined.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Do not call out today﴾

O polytheists, for one regret: that is, one time. Rather, call out for it many times. It was said: ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction﴾ because "thubur" is a verbal noun, and verbal nouns are not made plural; they are described by the length of their duration and their frequency, as one says: "he sat a long sitting" and "he ate a lot of food."

- Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first to be clothed in a garment of Fire will be Iblis; he will place it upon his brows and drag it behind him, and his offspring behind him, and he will say: 'Woe to me!' and they will call out: 'Woe to them!' Then it will be said: ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions.﴾"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 15–16:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the God-fearing have been promised? It shall be a reward and a destination for them."﴾ (15) ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding forever. It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for.﴾ (16)

His Exalted remembrance says: Say, O Muhammad, to these who deny the Hour: Is this Fire, whose description and the description of its people your Lord has set forth for you, better? Or the orchard of eternity, whose bliss endures and does not perish, which He promised to whoever feared Him in this world by obeying Him in what He commanded and forbade? As for His saying, ﴿It shall be a reward and a destination for them﴾, it means: the Garden of eternity was a reward for the God-fearing for their deeds toward God in this world by obeying Him, and a recompense for their taqwa (God-consciousness) of Him, and a destination for them; that is, a destination for the God-fearing who arrive at it in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish﴾

It means: for these God-fearing people, in the Garden of eternity which God promised them, is whatever they wish of what the souls desire and the eyes delight in, ﴿abiding forever﴾ therein; that is, remaining therein eternally, never departing from it, and its bliss never departing from them.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for﴾

That is because the believers asked their Lord for it in this world when they said: ﴿And give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾. God, blessed and exalted, says: The giving by God to the believers of the Garden of eternity, whose description He set forth, in the Hereafter, was a promise which God made to them in return for their obedience to Him in this world and their asking Him for it.

And the people of interpretation have said what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for﴾, he said: They asked Him who promised them, and they claimed it.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for﴾, he said: They asked Him for it in this world; they sought it, so He gave them His promise when they asked Him to give it to them, and He gave it to them. Thus it was a promise to be asked for, just as He determined the provisions of the servants on the earth before He created them, making them sustenance for those who ask, determining it upon their asking. And he recited: ﴿And He determined therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask﴾.

Some of the grammarians have directed the meaning of His saying ﴿a promise to be asked for﴾ toward the sense that it means a binding promise, because what is asked for is binding even if it is not requested, like a debt. They cite the Arabs' saying: "I will give you a thousand as a promise to be asked for," meaning "owed to you," so you ask for it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 15–16:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the God-fearing have been promised? It shall be a reward and a destination for them."﴾ (15) ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding forever. It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for.﴾ (16)

His Exalted remembrance says: Say, O Muhammad, to these who deny the Hour: Is this Fire, whose description and the description of its people your Lord has set forth for you, better? Or the orchard of eternity, whose bliss endures and does not perish, which He promised to whoever feared Him in this world by obeying Him in what He commanded and forbade? As for His saying, ﴿It shall be a reward and a destination for them﴾, it means: the Garden of eternity was a reward for the God-fearing for their deeds toward God in this world by obeying Him, and a recompense for their taqwa (God-consciousness) of Him, and a destination for them; that is, a destination for the God-fearing who arrive at it in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish﴾

It means: for these God-fearing people, in the Garden of eternity which God promised them, is whatever they wish of what the souls desire and the eyes delight in, ﴿abiding forever﴾ therein; that is, remaining therein eternally, never departing from it, and its bliss never departing from them.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for﴾

That is because the believers asked their Lord for it in this world when they said: ﴿And give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾. God, blessed and exalted, says: The giving by God to the believers of the Garden of eternity, whose description He set forth, in the Hereafter, was a promise which God made to them in return for their obedience to Him in this world and their asking Him for it.

And the people of interpretation have said what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for﴾, he said: They asked Him who promised them, and they claimed it.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for﴾, he said: They asked Him for it in this world; they sought it, so He gave them His promise when they asked Him to give it to them, and He gave it to them. Thus it was a promise to be asked for, just as He determined the provisions of the servants on the earth before He created them, making them sustenance for those who ask, determining it upon their asking. And he recited: ﴿And He determined therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask﴾.

Some of the grammarians have directed the meaning of His saying ﴿a promise to be asked for﴾ toward the sense that it means a binding promise, because what is asked for is binding even if it is not requested, like a debt. They cite the Arabs' saying: "I will give you a thousand as a promise to be asked for," meaning "owed to you," so you ask for it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 17:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day He gathers them, and those they worshipped besides Allah, He will say: "Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?"﴾

His words, exalted is He, mean: And (remember) the day We gather these deniers of the Hour, the worshippers of idols, and those they worshipped besides Allah from among the angels, mankind and jinn.

As related:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿And on the day He gathers them and those they worshipped besides Allah﴾ and ﴿He will say: "Did you lead these, My servants, astray"﴾ He said: Isa, Uzayr and the angels.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar to it.

The readers (qurra') differed in the recitation of this. Abu Ja'far the reciter and Abdullah ibn Kathir recited ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَيَقُولُ﴾ all with the letter ya' (yahshuruhum, yaqulu), meaning: "And the day your Lord gathers them, and gathers what they worshipped besides Allah, and He will say." The majority of the Kufan readers recited ﴿نَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾ with the letter nun (nahshuruhum), then ﴿فَنَقُولُ﴾ (faqulu). Nafi' also recited it this way.

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is to say: they are two well-known recitations with close meanings, and whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

* *

As for His words: ﴿فَيَقُولُ أَأَنْتُمْ أَضْلَلْتُمْ عِبَادِي هَؤُلاءِ﴾

He says: Then Allah will say to those whom these polytheists used to worship besides Allah: "Did you lead these My servants astray?" That is: "Did you remove them from the path of guidance, and call them to error and misguidance until they wandered and perished, or did they themselves stray from the way?" That is: "Or did My servants themselves stray from the path of right guidance and truth, and take the road to ruin?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 18:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿They will say: Glory be to You! It was not for us to take any protectors besides You, but You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the Reminder, and they were a people ruined.﴾ (18)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The angels whom these polytheists used to worship besides Allah, and Jesus, will say: "Exalted are You, O our Lord, and free are You from what these polytheists attribute to You. It was not fitting for us to take, besides You, any protectors whom we would befriend; You are our Protector besides them. But You gave them enjoyment with wealth, O our Lord, in this world, and health, until they forgot the Remembrance, and they were a people destroyed, upon whom wretchedness and abandonment had prevailed."

The exegetes have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿but You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the Reminder, and they were a people ruined﴾ he said: "a people whose deeds have perished while they were in the world, and who had no righteous deeds."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿and they were a people ruined﴾ he said: "destroyed."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and they were a people ruined﴾ he said: "destroyed."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and they were a people ruined﴾, he said: "They are those in whom there is no good." Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and they were a people ruined﴾: "He says: they have no good in them at all." Al-Bur: that in which there is no good at all.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿It was not for us to take any protectors besides You﴾. The majority of the readers of the principal cities recited ﴿nattakhidha﴾ with a fatha on the nun, except al-Hasan and Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa', who recited it ﴿nuttakhadha﴾ with a damma on the nun. Those who read it with a fatha took the meaning we have explained in its interpretation, that the angels, Jesus, and those worshipped besides Allah among the believers are those who disavowed having had any protector other than Allah, may He be remembered. As for those who read it with a damma on the nun, they directed the meaning of the speech to mean that the worshipped ones in the world only disavowed before Allah that it should have been for them to be worshipped besides Allah, may His praise be exalted, as Allah related about Jesus, that he said when it was said: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah"? He said: Glory be to You! It was not for me to say what I have no right to say... I said to them only what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who read it with a fatha on the nun, for three reasons. The first: the consensus of the readers upon it. The second: Allah, may His praise be exalted, mentioned a parallel of this story in Surah Saba', saying: ﴿And on the Day He gathers them all, then He says to the angels, "Did these used to worship you?" They say: Glory be to You! You are our Protector, not them﴾. So He related that the angels, when asked about the worship of those who worshipped them, disavowed before Allah their having been taken as protectors, and said to their Lord: "You are our Protector besides them." This clarifies the soundness of the reading of one who recites ﴿It was not for us to take any protectors besides You﴾ with the meaning: "It was not for us to take them as protectors besides You." The third: the Arabs do not use this "min" which enters into negation except with nouns, and do not use it with predicates; they do not say "I did not see your brother from a man," but they say "I did not see from anyone" and "I do not have from a man." Here it has entered upon "protectors," which is in the position of the predicate, and had there not been "min" in it, it would have been a good construction. As for al-Bur: it is a verbal noun that is singular and also the plural of bA'ir, as it is said: "Their dwellings became bur," meaning empty with nothing in them. From it is the saying of Ibn al-Za'ara: 

"O Messenger of the King, my tongue is one who mends what I have torn, while I am bur."

[The verse is by Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari, who said it when he converted to Islam at the conquest of Makkah. Raatiq: one who repairs what he has spoiled; the root of ratq is sealing a torn garment by mending what has been cut from it. Fataqtu: I spoiled from religion; every sin is a tearing and rending, and every repentance is a mending. Bur: ruined. It is said: a man bur and ba'ir, and a people bur; the root of bur is the verbal noun of baara yabuuru buuran, then it was applied as a description and kept the singular form because verbal nouns are not pluralized.]

It has also been said that "bur" is a verbal noun, like "adl, zur, and qat'," which is not dualized, pluralized, or feminized, and that what is meant by "bur" in this place is that the deeds of these disbelievers were void, because they were not for Allah, as we mentioned from Ibn Abbas.

The commentary on the verse: Concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He, ﴿So they have indeed denied you in what you say, and you cannot avert [the punishment] or find help﴾ (19).

God, exalted is His remembrance, says, informing of what He will say to the polytheists when those whom they worshipped besides God in the world disown them: "They have indeed denied you, O disbelievers, those whom you claimed had led you astray and invited you to worship them, in what you say," meaning, in your statements. He says: they denied you by your lies.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So they have indeed denied you in what you say﴾: God says to those who used to worship Jesus, Ezra and the angels, they deny the polytheists.

Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So they have indeed denied you in what you say﴾, he said: Jesus, Ezra and the angels, they deny the polytheists by their words.

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning the interpretation of this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿So they have indeed denied you in what you say, and you cannot avert [the punishment] or find help﴾: "They denied you in what you say," by what came from God, which the prophets brought and the believers believed in, and these denied it. Ibn Zayd thus directed the interpretation of His words ﴿So they have indeed denied you﴾ to: "So they have indeed denied you, O believers, who are denying what Muhammad brought from God, in what you say of the truth." This would be a report about those who denied the disbelievers in their claim that they invited them to misguidance and commanded them to it. However, the saying of Mujahid that we mentioned from him is more fitting and more preferable, since it occurs within the context of a report about them. Our reading of this is ﴿they have indeed denied you in what you say﴾ with the letter ta, according to the interpretation we have mentioned, because the authoritative readers of the cities agree upon it. It has been transmitted from some of them that he read ﴿in what they say﴾ with the letter ya, meaning: they have indeed denied you by their statement.

As for His words, exalted is His praise, ﴿and you cannot avert [the punishment] or find help﴾: it means, these disbelievers cannot avert the punishment of God from themselves when it descends upon them, nor can they help themselves against God when He punishes and chastises them.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So they cannot avert [it] or find help﴾: the polytheists cannot do it.

Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and you cannot avert [the punishment] or find help﴾: the polytheists. Ibn Jurayj said: they cannot avert the punishment from them, nor help themselves.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿So they cannot avert [it] or find help﴾: they cannot turn away from themselves the punishment that descended upon them when they denied, nor can they be helped. He said: On the Day of Resurrection, when the creatures are gathered, a herald will call out: "What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?" He said: Whoever was worshipped besides God will not help the one who worshipped him today. And those who worshipped besides God said: His god whom he worshipped besides God will not help him today. Then God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Rather, they today are submitting [in surrender]﴾, and he recited the saying of God, exalted is His praise: ﴿If you have a plot, then plot against Me﴾.

It has been related from Ibn Mas'ud concerning this:

Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, saying: al-Qasim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, who said: It is in the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: ﴿So they cannot avert for you [any] turning away﴾. If this report from him is sound, then the interpretation that Ibn Zayd gave of His words ﴿So they have indeed denied you in what you say﴾ is correct, and His words ﴿So they have indeed denied you﴾ become a report about the polytheists that they denied the believers. Its interpretation then would be: ﴿So they cannot avert for you, O Muhammad, any turning away﴾: these disbelievers cannot turn you away from the truth that God has guided you to, nor can they help themselves from the trial they are in, because of their denial of you.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He, ﴿And whoever among you does wrong, We will make him taste a great punishment﴾ (19).

God, exalted is His remembrance, says to the believers in Him: ﴿And whoever among you does wrong﴾, O believers, meaning by His words ﴿whoever does wrong﴾: whoever associates [partners] with God and thereby wrongs himself, We will make him taste a great punishment, like what We said We would make taste to those who denied the Hour.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His words ﴿And whoever among you does wrong﴾: he associates [partners], ﴿We will make him taste a great punishment﴾.

Al-Hasan told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And whoever among you does wrong﴾: it is shirk.

On the words of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Wa-ma arsalna qablaka mina al-mursalin illa innahum la-ya'kuluna al-ta'am wa-yamshuna fi al-aswaq wa-ja'alna ba'dakum li-ba'din fitnah, a-tasbirun? wa-kana rabbuka basiran﴾ (25:20).

This is an argument from God, dhikruhu, to His Prophet against the polytheists of his people who said: ﴿What is this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?﴾ And it is God's reply to them, as He, jalla thana'uhu, says to them: O Muhammad, what do these sayers deny, who say, "What is this Messenger that he eats food?" – [what do they deny] of your eating food and walking in the markets, while you are a messenger of God? They knew that We did not send any messengers before you except that they ate food and walked in the markets, just as you eat and walk. So they have no argument against you in what they said of that.

If someone says: "The word min (from) is not in the recitation, so how do you say the meaning of the speech is: 'except that from [among them] they eat food'?" It is said in reply: We say regarding that, its meaning is: the hā' and mīm in His saying innahum (that they) are pronouns referring to unmentioned nouns, and they must refer back to those whom they stand for. The mention and expression of min in the speech was omitted, being sufficiently indicated by His saying ﴿of the messengers﴾, just as the expression of min was dispensed with in His saying ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾. There is no doubt that the meaning is: "There is none of us but one who has a known station," just as it is said ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾, meaning: "And there is none of you but one who will come to it." So His saying innahum la-ya'kuluna al-ta'am is a relative clause (ṣila) for the omitted min, as one says in speech: "I did not send to you of the people except one who indeed conveys to you the message," where "indeed he conveys to you the message" is the relative clause for min.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We made some of you a trial for others﴾

He, dhikruhu, says: We test you, O people, through one another. We made this one a prophet and singled him out with the message, and this one a king and singled him out with worldly life, and this one a poor man and withheld worldly life from him, in order to test the poor man by his patience over what was withheld from him of what the rich man was given, and the king by his patience over what the Messenger was given of honour, and how each one of them is content with what was given to him and apportioned to him, and with his obedience to his Lord despite what was withheld from him of what was given to another. He says: For this reason I did not give Muhammad worldly life, and made him seek livelihood in the markets. And I test you, O people, and examine your obedience to your Lord and your answering His Messenger to what he calls you to, without any worldly gain that you hope for from Muhammad to give you upon following him, for if I had given him worldly life, many of you would have hastened to follow him out of greed for his worldly life, that you might obtain some of it.

Those of the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said in interpreting this.

Mention of those who said that:

Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', he said: ʿAbd al-Quddus narrated to me, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿And We made some of you a trial for others﴾ ... the verse, [he] says: This blind man says, "If God willed, He would have made me sighted like so-and-so"; this poor man says, "If God willed, He would have made me rich like so-and-so"; this sick man says, "If God willed, He would have made me healthy like so-and-so."

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿And We made some of you a trial for others, will you be patient?﴾ He said: He withholds from this one and expands for that one, so he says: "My Lord did not give me what He gave so-and-so," and [one is] tested with illness likewise, so he says: "My Lord did not make me healthy like so-and-so," and similar trials, so that He may know who among them is patient and who is impatient.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah related to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, as al-Tabari sees it, from ʿIkrimah, or from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: And there was revealed to him, concerning their saying: ﴿What is this Messenger that eats food and walks in the markets?⦆ ... the verse: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We made some of you a trial for others: will you be patient?﴾ That is: I made some of you a trial for others, so that you would be patient over what you hear from them and see of their opposition, and follow guidance without my giving them worldly life for it. Had I willed to make the world accompany My messengers so that they would not oppose, I would have done so, but I wished to test the servants through you and to test you through them.

On His saying: ﴿And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾

He says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is Seeing of the one who is impatient and the one who is patient over what he is tested with of trials.

As follows:

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾ – indeed your Lord is Seeing of the one who is impatient and the one who is patient.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 21–22:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Why were the angels not sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?" Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed greatly in insolence.﴾

His exalted remembrance says: The polytheists said, "Those who do not fear meeting Us, nor dread Our punishment," "Why has God not sent down angels to us, to inform us that Muhammad is right in what he says, and that what he has brought us is true, or [why] do we not see our Lord, so that He informs us of that?" As His exalted praise said, reporting about them: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾. Then He said after that: ﴿Or you bring God and the angels as a guarantee﴾. God says: Indeed, those who uttered this statement have become arrogant within themselves, and exalted themselves, ﴿and have transgressed greatly in insolence﴾, meaning: they exceeded the limit in arrogance by their saying that.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said in explaining this.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The disbelievers of Quraysh said: ﴿Why were the angels not sent down to us?﴾ so that they would inform us that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. ﴿They have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed in insolence﴾. Because "ʿataa" is from the roots with waw, its verbal noun is brought out in its original form with waw. And it is said in Surah Maryam: ﴿And I have reached extreme old age (kibar), ʿitiyyan﴾. This was said in that manner in order to match the verbal nouns with the plural forms of nouns in this respect, as in their saying: "qaʿada quʿūdan" (he sat, a sitting), and "hum qawmun quʿūd" (they are a sitting people). When this was so, and the one who is ʿatī would have its plural as ʿitiyy by analogy with the singular, [the verbal noun] was sometimes made to match its plural and sometimes returned to its original form.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no glad tidings that Day for the criminals, and they will say, "A forbidding, forbidden [barrier]."﴾

His exalted remembrance says: On the day when those who said, ﴿Why were the angels not sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?﴾ see the angels confirming Muhammad, there will be no good tidings for them that day. ﴿And they will say, "A forbidding, forbidden [barrier]"﴾, meaning that the angels will say to the criminals, "A forbidding, forbidden [barrier]," i.e., forbidden and prohibited for you today is that glad tidings from God should be yours. From the root ḥ-j-r comes the verse of al-Mutalammis:

*Her longing turned to the farthest palm, so I said to her:*
*"Ḥijr ḥarām, is that not the calamity (al-dahārīs)?"* [[The verse is by al-Mutalammis Jarir ibn Abd al-Masih (from Mu'jam ma Asta'jam by Abu Ubayd al-Bakri, entry: Rasm Nakhla). "Hanna" means longed. In al-Lisan (dahrasa) it is written "hajjat". Nakhla al-Quswa is a place about one night from Mecca. It is also said that there are two: Nakhla al-Shamiyya and Nakhla al-Yamaniyya; the Shamiyya is a valley descending from al-Ghamir, and the Yamaniyya is a valley descending from the bottom of Qarn al-Manazil, which is the road from Yemen to Mecca. Ḥijr, with the ḥa vowelled in three ways, means ḥarām, and in al-Bakri's Mu'jam: "bassal ʿalayka," which is also forbidden. Al-Dahārīs is the plural of dahras, with the dal vowelled in three ways, and means calamity (from al-Lisan). The verse is one of the evidences of Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 167 of the University photocopy no. 26059), and the author took it from him.]]

From it comes their saying: "The judge placed a ḥajr upon so-and-so" (i.e., imposed restraint), and "so-and-so placed a ḥajr upon his family." And from it comes Ḥijr al-Kaʿba, because no one enters it during circumambulation; rather, one circumambulates behind it. And from it is the saying of another:

*So I resolved to approach her with a muḥajjar,*
*and such a woman is approached with a muḥajjar.* [[The verse is by Humayd ibn Thawr al-Hilali (al-Lisan: ḥ-j-r; the Diwan, Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyya edition, p. 84). Mention of those who said that:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 21–22:

His exalted remembrance says: The polytheists said, "Those who do not fear meeting Us, nor dread Our punishment," "Why has God not sent down angels to us, to inform us that Muhammad is right in what he says, and that what he has brought us is true, or [why] do we not see our Lord, so that He informs us of that?" As His exalted praise said, reporting about them: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾. Then He said after that: ﴿Or you bring God and the angels as a guarantee﴾. God says: Indeed, those who uttered this statement have become arrogant within themselves, and exalted themselves, ﴿and have transgressed greatly in insolence﴾, meaning: they exceeded the limit in arrogance by their saying that.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said in explaining this.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The disbelievers of Quraysh said: ﴿Why were the angels not sent down to us?﴾ so that they would inform us that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. ﴿They have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed in insolence﴾. Because "ʿataa" is from the roots with waw, its verbal noun is brought out in its original form with waw. And it is said in Surah Maryam: ﴿And I have reached extreme old age (kibar), ʿitiyyan﴾. This was said in that manner in order to match the verbal nouns with the plural forms of nouns in this respect, as in their saying: "qaʿada quʿūdan" (he sat, a sitting), and "hum qawmun quʿūd" (they are a sitting people). When this was so, and the one who is ʿatī would have its plural as ʿitiyy by analogy with the singular, [the verbal noun] was sometimes made to match its plural and sometimes returned to its original form.

*Her longing turned to the farthest palm, so I said to her:*
*"Ḥijr ḥarām, is that not the calamity (al-dahārīs)?"* [[The verse is by al-Mutalammis Jarir ibn Abd al-Masih (from Mu'jam ma Asta'jam by Abu Ubayd al-Bakri, entry: Rasm Nakhla). On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest.﴾

His words, mentioned be He, mean: ﴿And We turned﴾, that is, We intended, toward what these criminals did ﴿of deeds﴾. Among its uses is the verse of the rajaz poet:

*"The misguided Kharijites advanced upon the servants of their Lord and said:*
*'Indeed your blood is lawful to us.'"*

[The rajaz verse is among the witnesses cited by Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 167, photographed copy of the University, 26059). "Qadima ila al-shay'" means he intended it and aimed at it. This is the point of evidence for the author.]

By "qadima" he means "intended."

Those who engaged in ta'wil (interpretation, i.e. tafsir) said the same as what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We turned﴾: he said, "We intended."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same. And regarding His words ﴿and made them scattered dust﴾, he says: "We made it void, because they did not do it for God; they did it for Satan."

*Al-haba'* (dust motes, a technical term for fine particles) is that which appears like dust when sunlight enters through an opening (kuwwa); the observer thinks it is dust, but it is nothing that hands can grasp or touch, and this is not seen in shade.

The people of ta'wil differed about its interpretation. Some said the same as what we have said about it.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrima, that he said regarding this verse ﴿scattered dust﴾: "The dust that is in the sun."

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And We turned to what they did of deeds and made them scattered dust﴾: "It is the ray in the opening of one of them; if he tries to grasp it, he cannot."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿scattered dust﴾: "It is the sunlight through the opening."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿scattered dust﴾: "I have not seen anything enter a house from the sun, entering through the opening, except that it is the haba'."

Others said: rather, it is what the winds blow away of dust, and what they scatter of the debris of trees, and the like.

Those who said that:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿scattered dust﴾: "It is what the wind blows away, scattering it."

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿scattered dust﴾: "It is what the wind scatters of the debris of this tree."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿scattered dust﴾: "Haba': dust."

Others said: it is poured-out water.

Those who said that:

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿scattered dust﴾: "It is said: poured-out water."

His words, glorified is His praise: ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest.﴾ His words, mentioned be He, mean: The people of the Garden on the Day of Resurrection are better in their place of settling, which is the place where they settle in their dwellings in the Garden, than the resting place of these polytheists who boast of their wealth and what they were given of the goods of this worldly life in this world, and finer for them in midday rest there.

If someone says: Is there a midday rest (qa'ila) in the Garden, so that it is said ﴿and finer in midday rest﴾ therein? It is said: The meaning of that is: and finer therein in settling, at the times of their midday rest in this world. This is because He mentioned that the people of the Garden in the Hereafter will experience only the amount of the time of the day from its beginning until the time of midday rest, until they settle their dwellings in the Garden. That is the meaning of His words ﴿and finer in midday rest﴾.

The narration from those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest﴾: he says, "They said in the chambers in the Garden, and their reckoning was that they were presented to their Lord in a single presentation, and that is the easy reckoning," and it is like His words: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, and he will return to his people joyful.﴾

- Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest﴾: he said, "They used to think that the reckoning of people on the Day of Resurrection would be finished at midday; then these would rest in the Garden and those in the Fire."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest﴾: he said, "The day does not reach midday until God judges between them, so the people of the Garden rest in the Garden and the people of the Fire rest in the Fire." He said: And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿Then indeed their resting place is toward the Blazing Fire.﴾

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest﴾: he said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "The reckoning from that is at its beginning, and the people said when they spoke in their dwellings in the Garden," and he recited ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest.﴾

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, that Sa'id al-Sawwaf narrated to him that it reached him that on the Day of Resurrection judgment will be passed on the believers until it is like the time between the afternoon prayer and sunset, and that they will rest in the gardens of the Garden until people are finished; that is the saying of God: ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: We have only said that the meaning of that is: better in resting place in the Garden than they were in the world, because God, mentioned be His praise, in His words ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest﴾ generalized all states of the Garden in the Hereafter as better in settling there, and the midday rest was among all the states of the people of the Fire. He did not specify that it is better than their states in the Fire rather than in the world, nor in the world rather than in the Hereafter. So it is necessary that it be general as our Lord, exalted is His praise, made it general. It is said: The companions of the Garden on the Day of Resurrection are better in resting place in the Garden than the people of the Fire in the world and the Hereafter, and finer than them in midday rest. And when that is its meaning, the corruption of the view of one who imagined that the preference of the people of the Garden in God's words ﴿better in resting place﴾ is in a manner other than the known usage of people's speech among themselves, in their saying: "This is better than this" and "This is finer than this," becomes clear.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest﴾: he said, "The day does not reach midday until God judges between them, so the people of the Garden rest in the Garden and the people of the Fire rest in the Fire." He said: And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿Then indeed their resting place is toward the Blazing Fire.﴾

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest﴾: he said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "The reckoning from that is at its beginning, and the people said when they spoke in their dwellings in the Garden," and he recited ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest.﴾

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, that Sa'id al-Sawwaf narrated to him that it reached him that on the Day of Resurrection judgment will be passed on the believers until it is like the time between the afternoon prayer and sunset, and that they will rest in the gardens of the Garden until people are finished; that is the saying of God: ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: We have only said that the meaning of that is: better in resting place in the Garden than they were in the world, because God, mentioned be His praise, in His words ﴿The companions of the Garden, that Day, will be better in resting place and finer in midday rest﴾ generalized all states of the Garden in the Hereafter as better in settling there, and the midday rest was among all the states of the people of the Fire. He did not specify that it is better than their states in the Fire rather than in the world, nor in the world rather than in the Hereafter. So it is necessary that it be general as our Lord, exalted is His praise, made it general. It is said: The companions of the Garden on the Day of Resurrection are better in resting place in the Garden than the people of the Fire in the world and the Hereafter, and finer than them in midday rest. And when that is its meaning, the corruption of the view of one who imagined that the preference of the people of the Garden in God's words ﴿better in resting place﴾ is in a manner other than the known usage of people's speech among themselves, in their saying: "This is better than this" and "This is finer than this," becomes clear.

The commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿And the day the sky is split open with clouds, and the angels are sent down in a descent﴾ (25) ﴿Sovereignty on that day belongs truly to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾ (26).

The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿tashaqqaqu﴾. The majority of the readers of the Hijaz recited it as ﴿wa-yawma tashsha��qu﴾ with the shin doubled, meaning "tatashaqqaqu" (is split open), so that they assimilated one of the two tā' into the shin and doubled it, as in His words: ﴿they cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾.

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as ﴿wa-yawma tashaqqaqu﴾ with the shin lightened, dispensing with one of the two tā'.

My view on this is that both are widely transmitted recitations among the regional readers, with one meaning, so whichever of them the reciter uses is correct. The meaning of the speech is: "and the day the sky is split open with clouds." It has been said that these are white clouds like the cloud that shaded the Children of Israel, and the bā' in His words ﴿with the clouds﴾ is in place of "ʿan" (from), just as you say "I shot from the bow," "with the bow," and "on the bow," with one meaning.

People of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And the day the sky is split open with clouds﴾, he said: it is the one in His words ﴿in canopies of clouds﴾, in which God comes on the Day of Resurrection, and it has never been for anyone except the Children of Israel. Ibn Jurayj said: the cloud in which God comes is a cloud, they claim, in Paradise.

He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Jalil, from Abu Hazim, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: God descends when He descends, and between Him and His creation are seventy veils, among them light, darkness and water, and the water makes a sound that unsettles hearts.

He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrimah regarding His words: ﴿God will come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels﴾, he said: and the angels around Him.

He said: Hajjaj told me, from Mubarak ibn Fadala, from ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: when this sky is split open, more angels descend from it than jinn and humankind. It is the Day of Meeting, the day when the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet. The people of the earth will say: "Our Lord has come," and they will say: "He has not come, but He is coming." Then the second sky splits open, then sky after sky, at a similar multiplied rate, up to the seventh sky, and more angels descend from it than all who descended from the heavens and from the jinn and humankind. He said: the Karubiyyun angels descend, then our Lord, blessed and exalted, comes in the eight bearers of the Throne, between the knee and the ankle of each angel is a journey of seventy years, and between his thigh and his shoulder is a journey of seventy years. He said: each of them has not contemplated the face of his companion, and each of them has his head between his breasts saying: "Glory to the King, the Holy." Over their heads is something spread out like a dome, and the Throne is above that. Then he stopped.

He said: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Harun ibn Thawwab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: the bearers of the Throne are eight; four of them say: "Glory to You, O God, and praise be to You; to You is praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge," and four say: "Glory to You, O God, and praise be to You; to You is praise for Your pardon after Your power."

He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: when the people of the earth look at the Throne descending upon them from above, their eyes are fixed on it, and their hearts tremble in their chests, and their hearts fly from their places in their chests up to their throats.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿And the day the sky is split open with clouds, and the angels are sent down in a descent﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, when the sky is split open with clouds, and the angels are sent down in a descent.

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And the day when the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾ [25:27] ﴿"Oh woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!"﴾ [25:28] ﴿"He had led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me. And Satan is ever to man a deserter."﴾ [25:29]

His, the Exalted, says: "And the day when the wrongdoer, the polytheist who associated others with his Lord, will bite on his hands, out of regret and remorse for what he neglected regarding God's right, and for having ruined himself through disbelief in Him by obeying his close friend who turned him away from the way of his Lord, saying: 'Oh, would that I had taken in the world, along with the Messenger, a way,'" meaning a path to salvation from God's punishment.
