- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn related to me, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf used to attend the Prophet (ﷺ), and ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt rebuked him, so this was revealed: ﴿And the day when the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾ ... to His saying ﴿a deserter﴾. He said: "The wrongdoer" is ʿUqbah, and "so-and-so, as a close friend" is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from al-Shaʿbi, concerning His saying: ﴿"Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!"﴾ He said: ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt was a close friend of Umayyah ibn Khalaf. Then ʿUqbah embraced Islam, so Umayyah said: "My face is forbidden to your face if you follow Muhammad and disbelieve." And it is he who said: ﴿"Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!"﴾.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah and ʿUthman al-Jazari, from Miqsam, concerning His saying: ﴿And the day when the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾ He said: ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt and Ubayy ibn Khalaf gathered, and they were close friends. One of them said to his companion: "I have been told that you came to Muhammad and listened to him. By God, I will not be pleased with you until you spit in his face and call him a liar." God did not give him power over that, so ʿUqbah was killed on the day of Badr by being put to death in cold blood [[It is said: "So-and-so was killed sabran" when he was brought forward and killed while seeing and looking on, and this is other than being killed in battle or by accident. al-Saqqa.]]. As for Ubayy ibn Khalaf, the Prophet (ﷺ) killed him with his own hand on the day of Uhud in the fighting. These are the two about whom God revealed: ﴿And the day when the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾.

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the day when the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿so-and-so as a close friend﴾. He said: It is Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who used to attend the Prophet (ﷺ), and ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt rebuked him.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And the day when the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾ He said: ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt invited a gathering in which was the Prophet (ﷺ) to a meal. The Prophet (ﷺ) refused to eat, and said: "I will not eat until you testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." He said: "Are you not going to eat until I bear witness?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." Then Umayyah ibn Khalaf met him and said: "Have you turned away?" He said: "Your brother is upon what you know, but I made food and he refused to eat until I said that, so I said it, and it was not from my own self."

Others said: By "so-and-so" is meant Satan.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿so-and-so as a close friend﴾. He said: Satan.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

And His saying: ﴿"He had led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me."﴾

His, may His praise be exalted, informs about this one who regrets what he had done in the world of disobedience to his Lord by obeying his close friend: "He led me astray from faith in the Qur'an, which is the Reminder, after it had come to me from God, and he turned me away from it." God says: ﴿And Satan is ever to man a deserter﴾, meaning: one who abandons him to whatever calamity befalls him, not rescuing him nor saving him.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the Messenger will say, "My Lord, my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾ (25:30) ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy among the criminals. And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and helper.﴾ (25:31)

His exalted mention says: And the Messenger said, on the Day when the wrongdoer bites his hands: "My Lord, my people, to whom You sent me to call them to Your oneness, have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed concerning the meaning of their taking the Qur'an as abandoned. Some of them said: their taking it was abandonment (hajr), through their speaking evil about it and their claim that it is magic and that it is poetry.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned﴾. He said: They abandon it by speech; they say: "It is magic."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And the Messenger said﴾... the verse: They abandon it by speech. Mujahid said, concerning His saying: ﴿arrogantly regarding it, conversing by night, speaking nonsense﴾ (23:67): "Arrogant in the city, gathered in assemblies, you abandon [it], by evil speech about the Qur'an that is not the truth."

Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿My people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned﴾. He said: They spoke about it what is not the truth. Have you not seen the sick person, when he raves, that he speaks what is not true?

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: a report about the polytheists, that they abandoned the Qur'an, turned away from it, and did not listen to it.

Those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And the Messenger said: My Lord, my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned﴾: They do not want to hear it, and when they are called to Allah they say, "No." He recited: ﴿and they forbid others from it and keep away from it﴾ (6:26). He said: They forbid [others] from it and keep far from it.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This view is more fitting as the interpretation of that, because Allah reported about them that they said: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it﴾ (41:26), and that is their abandonment of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy among the criminals﴾

His exalted mention says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Just as We have made for you, O Muhammad, enemies from the polytheists of your people, so too have We made for every prophet We have sent before you an enemy from the polytheists of his people. You were not singled out from among them by this. He means: so be patient with what reaches you from them, just as the resolute messengers (ulu al-azm) among Our messengers were patient before you.

The people of ta'wil said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy among the criminals﴾: He is assuring Muhammad (ﷺ) that He is appointing for him an enemy among the criminals, just as He appointed for those before him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and helper﴾

His exalted mention says to His Prophet: And sufficient for you, O Muhammad, is your Lord as a guide, who will guide you to the truth and show you the right course; and as a helper: that is, a helper for you against your enemies. He means: do not let your enemies among the polytheists frighten you, for I am your helper against them. So be patient with My command, and proceed to convey My message to them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 32:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" Thus it is, that We may strengthen your heart thereby; and We have recited it in measured recitation.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾ in Allah ﴿say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him﴾ — meaning: why was the Qur'an not sent down upon Muhammad ﷺ ﴿all at once?﴾ — as the Torah was sent down upon Moses all at once?" Allah said: ﴿Thus it is, that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾ — by sending it down to you verse after verse, and thing after thing, so that We may strengthen your heart thereby, We have sent it down.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" Thus it is, that We may strengthen your heart thereby; and We have recited it in measured recitation.﴾ He said: Allah would send down to him a verse, and when the Prophet of Allah had learned it, another verse would be sent down so that he might teach him the Book by heart, and so that his heart would be strengthened thereby.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" as the Torah was sent down upon Moses﴾ He said: ﴿Thus it is, that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾ He said: The Qur'an was sent down to him as a response to their saying, so that Muhammad would know that Allah answers the people in accordance with what they say, with the truth. And by His saying ﴿that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾ He means: that We may make firm the resolve of your heart and the certainty of your soul, and give you courage thereby.

And His saying: ﴿and We have recited it in measured recitation﴾

He says: and We taught it to you thing after thing, until you memorize it. Tartil in recitation means: deliberateness and steadiness.

Those of the interpreters said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, who said: Hushaym narrated to us, who said: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿and We have recited it in measured recitation﴾ He said: It was sent down in parts.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿and We have recited it in measured recitation﴾ He said: It would be sent down one verse, two verses, and several verses, as a response to them when they asked about something, which Allah sent down as an answer to them and as a refutation of what they said against the Prophet. And between its beginning and its end was about twenty years.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿and We have recited it in measured recitation﴾ He said: Between the beginning of what was sent down of the Qur'an and its end, it was sent down to him for forty [years], and the Prophet ﷺ died after sixty-two or sixty-three [years].

Others said: the meaning of tartil is clarification and explanation.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and We have recited it in measured recitation﴾ He said: We explained it as an explanation, and he recited: ﴿and recite the Qur'an in measured recitation﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verses 33–34:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will not bring you any comparison but that We will bring you the truth and better explanation (tafsir).﴾ [25:33] ﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell — those are worse in position and more astray in way.﴾ [25:34]

His exalted remembrance says: And those polytheists, O Muhammad, will not bring you any parable they coin, but that We will bring you of the truth, by which We will nullify what they have brought, and [bring] better than it in explanation.

As for:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And they will not bring you any comparison but that We will bring you the truth﴾, he said: "The Book, by which you refute what they have brought of the parables they have brought, and better explanation."

By His saying ﴿and better explanation﴾ He means: better than what they brought of the parable in clarity and detail.

And in the same manner as what we have said, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿and better explanation﴾, he said: "better in detail."

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and better explanation﴾, he said: "clarification."

* I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿and better explanation﴾: "detail."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell — those are worse in position﴾

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet: These polytheists, O Muhammad, who say to you, ﴿Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?﴾ and whoever is upon the same disbelief in Allah as they are upon, those who will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on their faces to Hell — they will be driven to Hell, worse in abode in this world and the Hereafter than the people of Paradise in Paradise, and more astray in the way in this world.

And in the same manner as what we have said, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell﴾, he said: "The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces." ﴿Those are worse in position﴾ than the people of Paradise ﴿and more astray in way﴾, he said: "way."

* Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shaybān narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell﴾, he said: "Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face?' He said: 'The One who made him walk on his feet is able to make him walk on his face.'"

* Abu Sufyan al-Ghanawi Yazid ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Khallad ibn Yahya al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: "Someone who heard Anas ibn Malik say informed me: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'How will He gather them on their faces?' He said: 'The One who gathers them on their feet is able to gather them on their faces.'"

* 'Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Abu Dawud, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: 'How will the people of the Fire be gathered on their faces?' He said: 'Indeed, the One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces.'"

* Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, saying: Hazm narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse, ﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell﴾, and they said: "O Prophet of Allah, how will they walk on their faces?" He said: "Have you considered: the One who made them walk on their feet, is He not able to make them walk on their faces?"

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn Zadhan informed us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Abu Khalid, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three categories: a category on beasts, a category on their feet, and a category on their faces." It was said: "How will they walk on their faces?" He said: "Indeed, the One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 35–36:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture and made his brother Aaron with him a minister﴾ [35] ﴿Then We said, "Go both of you to the people who denied Our signs." Then We destroyed them with complete destruction﴾ [36].

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), threatening the polytheists of his people for their disbelief in God and their denial of His Messenger, and warning them of the descent of His vengeance upon them, like that which befell the nations before them that denied their messengers: ﴿And We certainly gave﴾ O Muhammad ﴿Moses the Scripture﴾, meaning the Torah, just as We gave you the Furqan (criterion, i.e., the Qur'an) ﴿and made his brother Aaron with him a minister﴾, meaning a helper and supporter. ﴿Then We said, "Go both of you to the people who denied Our signs"﴾. He says: We said to them both: Go to Pharaoh and his people, who denied Our proofs and Our evidences, ﴿then We destroyed them with complete destruction﴾. In the speech there is an omitted element that is dispensed with by the indication of what has been mentioned, namely: they went and they denied them both, so We destroyed them at that time.

In the speech there is an omitted element that is dispensed with by the indication of what has been mentioned, namely: they went and they denied them both, so We destroyed them at that time.

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And the people of Noah when they denied the Messengers, We drowned them, and made them a sign for mankind, and We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.﴾ (25:37)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The people of Noah, when they denied Our messengers and rejected what they brought them of the truth, We drowned them by the flood. ﴿And We made them a sign for mankind﴾, meaning: We made their drowning and destruction an admonition and a lesson for people, by which they may take heed. ﴿And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment﴾, meaning: We have prepared for those among the disbelievers in Allah a painful punishment in the Hereafter, in addition to the punishment that befell them of swift retribution in this world.

* *

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And 'Ad and Thamud, and the companions of the Rass, and generations between them, many.﴾ (25:38) ﴿And to each We presented examples, and each We destroyed with complete destruction.﴾ (25:39)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We also destroyed 'Ad, Thamud, and the companions of the Rass.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., exegesis) differed regarding the companions of the Rass. Some of them said: The companions of the Rass were from Thamud.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿and the companions of the Rass﴾: "A town of Thamud."

Others said: Rather, it is a town in al-Yamama called al-Falj. [[In Taj al-'Arus: "It is said (fulj): a land. From it comes the name for the road that starts from Basra to al-Yamama: the road of Batn Fulj." End.]]

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, he said: Qatada said: "al-Rass is a town in al-Yamama called al-Falj."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ikrima said: "The companions of the Rass at al-Falj are the companions of Ya-Sin."

Others said: They are a people who buried their prophet in a well.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrima, he said: "The Rass was a well into which they buried their prophet."

Others said: It is a well that was called al-Rass.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and the companions of the Rass﴾: "It is a well that was called al-Rass."

Muhammad ibn 'Umara narrated to me, he said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿and the companions of the Rass﴾: "al-Rass is a well over which there was a people."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct view on this is the view of those who said: They were a people who were at a well. This is because al-Rass in the speech of the Arabs means every excavated thing such as a well, a grave, and the like. Among its uses is the words of the poet:

You have preceded to the water-drawing of the Bahili band, the Tanabila, who dig al-Rissas. [[The verse is by al-Nabigha al-Ja'di (Lisan: rass). Al-Farat (with a fatha on the ra) means: people who go ahead to the water before arrival, preparing for them the ropes and buckets, filling the troughs and drawing water for them (from Lisan). Al-Bahili: one who wanders without work. Al-Tanabila is the plural of tunbul, on the pattern of ja'far, meaning a short man; perhaps it is a metaphor for slowness and inability to work. Al-rissas is the plural of rass, which is an ancient well or a mine (a pit from which metals such as iron and the like are extracted). The author cited it to show that, according to the Arabs, everything excavated, such as a well, grave, or mine, is a rass.]]

He means that they dig into mines. I know of no people who had a story because of a pit, mentioned by Allah in His Book, except the People of the Trench (ashab al-ukhdud). If they are the ones meant by His words ﴿and the companions of the Rass﴾, we will mention their account, God willing, when we reach Surat al-Buruj. If they are other than them, we know of no account of them, except what came in a part of the report about them: that they were a people who buried their prophet in a pit.

Except what:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of the people to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection is the black slave." That is because Allah, blessed and exalted, sent a prophet to the people of a town, and none of its people believed except that black man. Then the people of the town attacked the Prophet, peace be upon him, dug a well for him, threw him into it, and then closed it over him with a huge rock. He said: That slave would go out to gather firewood on his back, then bring his firewood and sell it, and with it buy food and drink, then bring it to that well, lift that rock, and Allah would help him to do so; he would lower his food and drink to him, then put the rock back as it was. He said: So it continued as long as Allah willed. Then one day he went out to gather firewood as he always did, collected his wood, bundled it, and finished; when he wished to carry it he felt drowsiness, lay down, and slept, and Allah struck upon his ear for seven years while he slept. Then he awoke, stretched, turned to his other side, lay down, and Allah struck upon his ear for seven more years. Then he awoke, carried his bundle, and did not think he had slept except for an hour of the day. He came to the town, sold his bundle, bought food and drink as he used to do, then went to the pit in its place where he had been, and searched for him but did not find him. His people had by then changed their attitude toward him, so they took him out, believed in him, and affirmed him. He said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, used to ask them about that black man: "What has become of him?" They would say: "We do not know," until Allah took the Prophet (ﷺ). Then Allah awakened the black man from his sleep after that, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, that black man is the first to enter Paradise." However, in this report Muhammad ibn Ka'b mentions from the Prophet (ﷺ) that they believed in their prophet and brought him out of his pit. Therefore they should not be the ones meant by His words ﴿and the companions of the Rass﴾, because Allah informed about the companions of the Rass that He destroyed them with destruction, unless they were destroyed by events they created after their prophet whom they brought out of the pit and believed in; in that case, this would be a possibility. ﴿And generations between them, many﴾, meaning: And We destroyed between the multiples of these nations which We named for you, many nations.

As:

al-Hasan ibn Shabib narrated to us, he said: Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Rafi', client of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "I asked in Medina my paternal uncle, among those who issue legal opinions, about the qarn (generation), and he held that a qarn is seventy years," and his uncle was 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', scribe of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, he said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, he said: "The qarn is forty years."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And to each We presented examples﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: All these nations that We destroyed, whether We named them for you or did not name them, We presented to them examples, meaning: We set forth for them parables, alerted them to Our proofs against them, and gave them excuse by means of lessons and admonitions. We did not destroy any nation except after conveying the warning to them fully.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and to each We presented examples﴾: "Each one had Allah's excuse made to it, then He took vengeance upon it."

* *

However, in this report Muhammad ibn Ka'b mentions from the Prophet (ﷺ) that they believed in their prophet and brought him out of his pit. Therefore they should not be the ones meant by His words ﴿and the companions of the Rass﴾, because Allah informed about the companions of the Rass that He destroyed them with destruction, unless they were destroyed by events they created after their prophet whom they brought out of the pit and believed in; in that case, this would be a possibility. ﴿And generations between them, many﴾, meaning: And We destroyed between the multiples of these nations which We named for you, many nations.

As:

al-Hasan ibn Shabib narrated to us, he said: Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Rafi', client of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "I asked in Medina my paternal uncle, among those who issue legal opinions, about the qarn (generation), and he held that a qarn is seventy years," and his uncle was 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', scribe of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, he said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, he said: "The qarn is forty years."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And to each We presented examples﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: All these nations that We destroyed, whether We named them for you or did not name them, We presented to them examples, meaning: We set forth for them parables, alerted them to Our proofs against them, and gave them excuse by means of lessons and admonitions. We did not destroy any nation except after conveying the warning to them fully.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and to each We presented examples﴾: "Each one had Allah's excuse made to it, then He took vengeance upon it."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And each We destroyed with complete destruction﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: All these whose matters We have mentioned to you, We uprooted them and destroyed them with punishment, annihilating them, and We destroyed them all.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿and each We destroyed with complete destruction﴾: "Allah destroyed each with punishment, complete destruction."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿and each We destroyed with complete destruction﴾: "Tatbir is in Nabataean (Aramaic)."

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words ﴿and each We destroyed with complete destruction﴾: "With punishment."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 40:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they have certainly passed by the town upon which was rained a rain of evil. Have they not been seeing it? Rather, they were not expecting a resurrection.﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And these people who took the Qur'an as something abandoned had certainly passed by the town upon which God rained a rain of evil, which is Sodom, the town of the people of Lot. "A rain of evil" is the stones that God rained down upon them, by which He destroyed them. As:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj (﴿And they have certainly passed by the town upon which was rained a rain of evil﴾), he said: "Stones. It is the town of the people of Lot, and its name is Sodom." Ibn Abbas said: "There were five towns. God destroyed four, and the fifth remained, and its name is Sa'wa. Sa'wa was not destroyed; its people did not do that deed. Sodom was the greatest of them, and it is where Lot alighted, and from it he was sent. Ibrahim ﷺ used to call out to them in counsel: 'O Sodom, a day from God is coming upon you; I forbid you to expose yourselves to the punishment of God.'" They claimed that Lot was the son of Ibrahim's brother, may the blessings of God be upon both of them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Have they not been seeing it?﴾

He, may His majesty be praised, says: Did not these polytheists, who have passed by the town upon which was rained a rain of evil, see that town and what descended upon it of God's punishment because its people denied their messengers, so that they would take heed and be mindful, and return in repentance from their disbelief and their denial of Muhammad ﷺ? ﴿Rather, they were not expecting a resurrection.﴾ God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: They did not deny Muhammad in what he brought them from God because they had not seen what befell the town described; rather, they denied him because they are a people who do not fear a resurrection after death, meaning that they do not believe in reward and punishment, nor do they believe in the establishment of the Hour, so that this would deter them from the acts of disobedience to God that they commit.

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Have they not been seeing it? Rather, they were not expecting a resurrection﴾: "Resurrection."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 25, verses 41–42:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they see you, they take you not except in mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ (41)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And when these polytheists, whose accounts I have related to you, see you, ﴿they take you not except in mockery﴾, meaning: they take you only as an object of ridicule, mocking you, saying: ﴿"Is this the one whom Allah has sent"﴾ to us ﴿as a messenger﴾ from among His creation?

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿"He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in adhering to them." And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in way.﴾ (42)

He, exalted is His remembrance, reports about these polytheists who used to mock the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they would say when they saw him: "He has nearly led us astray from our gods that we worship, turning us away from their worship, had we not been patient with them and firm in worshipping them." ﴿And they will know when they see the punishment﴾: He, whose praise is majestic, says: it will become clear to them when they witness the punishment of Allah descending upon them for their worship of the gods, ﴿who is further astray in way﴾: meaning, who has strayed further from the path of guidance and taken the course of ruin, you or they?

And in agreement with what we have said regarding the interpretation of His saying, ﴿had we not been steadfast in adhering to them﴾, the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in adhering to them﴾: he said: "We would have been firm in them."

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verses 43–46:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god? Would you then be a guardian over him? Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are only like livestock; rather, they are further astray from the way.﴾ (43–44)

He, exalted is His remembrance, means: ﴿Have you seen﴾ O Muhammad ﴿him who takes his god﴾ to be his desire, which he covets. That is because a man among the polytheists would worship a stone, and when he saw something better than it, he would cast it away and take up the other to worship. So his deity and god was whatever he chose for himself. Therefore He, whose praise is exalted, said: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god? Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾ That is, He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Would you, O Muhammad, be a watcher over his actions, given his great ignorance? ﴿Or do you think﴾ O Muhammad that most of these polytheists ﴿hear﴾ what is recited to them, so that they heed it, ﴿or understand﴾ what they witness of the proofs of God, so that they comprehend? ﴿They are only like livestock﴾ meaning: they are no more than beasts that do not grasp what is said to them nor understand it. ﴿Rather, they are further astray from the way﴾ because beasts are guided to their pastures and submit to their masters, whereas these disbelievers do not obey their Lord, nor do they give thanks for the blessing of the One who bestowed favours upon them; rather they deny it, and they disobey the One who created and originated them.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade? Had He willed, He would have made it still. Then We made the sun its indicator. (45) Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal.﴾ (46)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Have you not seen﴾ O Muhammad ﴿how﴾ your Lord ﴿extends the shade﴾, and it is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun.

The interpreters have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade﴾ — he said: He extended it between the dawn prayer and the rising of the sun.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade, and had He willed, He would have made it still﴾ — he said: The shade is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun.

- Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay' related to us, he said: Abu Mihsan related to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, he said: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade﴾ — he said: what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿how He extended the shade﴾ — he said: the shade of the morning before the sun rises.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, he said: The shade: the shade of the morning.

 He said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Ikrimah, regarding His words: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade﴾ — he said: He extended it from the break of dawn to the rising of the sun.

- I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade﴾ — he means: from the morning prayer to the rising of the sun.

* *

His words: ﴿Had He willed, He would have made it still﴾

He says: Had He willed, He would have made it perpetual, which does not cease, extended, which the sun does not remove or diminish.

The interpreters have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Muawiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Had He willed, He would have made it still﴾ — he says: perpetual.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Had He willed, He would have made it still﴾ — he said: the sun does not reach it and it does not cease.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Had He willed, He would have made it still﴾ — he said: it does not cease.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Had He willed, He would have made it still﴾ — he said: perpetual, not ceasing.

* *

And His words: ﴿Then We made the sun its indicator﴾

He, whose praise is exalted, says: Then We showed you, O people, by the sun's abolishing it when it rises over it, that it is a creation among the creatures of your Lord, which He brings into being when He wills and annihilates when He desires. The pronoun in His words "over it" refers to the shade; its meaning is: then We made the sun over the shade an indicator. It has been said: the meaning of its indicating it is that, had there not been the sun which abolishes it, it would not be known to be a thing, since things are only known by their opposites, like the sweet which is known only by the sour, and the cold by the hot, and what is similar to that.

The interpreters have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Muawiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Then We made the sun its indicator﴾ — he says: the rising of the sun.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Then We made the sun its indicator﴾ — he said: it encompasses it.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, the same.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God: ﴿Then We made the sun its indicator﴾ — he said: it removed that shade and took it away.

And His words: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Then We withdrew that indicator, which is the sun over the shade, to Us, withdrawing it secretly and swiftly, by the shade that We bring in the evening.

The interpreters have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾ — he said: the sun encompassed the shade.

It has been said that the pronoun in His words "Then We withdraw it to Us" refers to the shade, and that the meaning of the statement is: Then We withdraw the shade to Us after the sun sets, because when the sun sets the extended shade disappears; they said: that is the time of its withdrawal.

The interpreters differed on the meaning of His words "gradual" (yasiran). Some of them said: its meaning is: swift.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Muawiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾ — he says: swift.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: a secret withdrawal.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi', from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾ — he said: secret.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said: Ibn Juraj said regarding ﴿a gradual withdrawal﴾ — he said: secret. He said: what lies between the sun and the shade is like a thread. "Yasir" is the form fa'il from "yusr," which in the speech of the Arabs means easy and light. The meaning of the statement, given that this is so, accords with what was related from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, since the ease of this withdrawal may come about through swiftness and secrecy. It has also been said that God only said "Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal" because the shade after the sun sets does not vanish all at once, nor does darkness take over all of it in one go; rather that shade is withdrawn secretly, bit by bit, and each part of it that is withdrawn is followed by a part of darkness.

That is because a man among the polytheists would worship a stone, and when he saw something better than it, he would cast it away and take up the other to worship. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 47:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who made for you the night as a garment, and sleep as rest, and made the day a resurrection.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He who extended the shade and then made the sun a guide over it, is the One who made the night for you, O people, a garment. Almighty God said ﴿made for you the night as a garment﴾ because He made it for His creatures as a shelter in which they hide and rest, so it becomes a covering for them with which they conceal themselves, just as they conceal themselves with the clothes they wear.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and sleep as rest﴾

He says: He made sleep for you as a repose by which your bodies find rest, and by which your limbs become still.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and made the day a resurrection﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He made the day a time of waking and life, from their saying "nashara al-mayyit" (the dead one was revived), as al-A'sha said:

"Until people say, from what they have seen: 'How strange is the dead one who is raised!'" [[The verse is by al-A'sha of Banu Qays ibn Tha'laba (Diwan, Cairo edition, with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 141). It comes from a poem in which he satirizes Alqama ibn Ulatha and praises Amir ibn al-Tufayl in the boasting contest that took place between them. Before the verse he says: "Had she (the beloved) leaned a dead man against her breast, he would have lived and not been carried to the grave." The verse is also cited in (Lisan al-Arab: nashr), where it says: "God revived the dead (nashara Allahu al-mayyita yanshuruhu nashran wa nushuran, and ansharaha), so that 'nashara al-mayyit' (with the dead as the subject) only means: He gave him life. Al-A'sha said: 'Until people say...' the verse." This is the place of evidence according to the author.]]

From the same root is God's saying: ﴿And they possess no power over death or life or resurrection.﴾

Mujahid used to say about the interpretation of this:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and made the day a resurrection﴾, he said: "It is when one is raised up in it."

* al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

We have chosen the interpretation we have chosen, that it follows His words ﴿and sleep as rest﴾ concerning the night. Given that this is so, describing the day as containing waking and resurrection from sleep is more fitting, since sleep is the brother of death. What Mujahid said is not far from the truth, because God informed that He made the day a means of livelihood, and in it is dispersal for livelihood; but "nushur" is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker "nashara," so it is more akin to being raised from death and sleep, just as the report from the Prophet ﷺ is authentic that when he woke in the morning and rose from his sleep he would say: "Praise be to God, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection."

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water, that We may give life thereby to a dead land and give it to drink, of what We have created, cattle and many people﴾ [25:48–49].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And Allah is the One who sends the winds that fertilize (the clouds), ﴿as glad tidings﴾, meaning life, or from al-hayā' (rain-bringing) and the rain which He sends down upon His servants. ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾, meaning: We send down from the clouds, which We produced by the winds, above you, O people, pure water. ﴿That We may give life thereby to a dead land﴾, meaning a barren, parched land that produces nothing. He said ﴿a dead land﴾ and did not say "dead (feminine)," because by this He intends a dead place and locality. ﴿And give it to drink﴾ of what We have created, ﴿cattle﴾ among the beasts, ﴿and many people﴾. The word ﴿anāsī﴾ is the plural of insān (human), and its plural is anāsī. He made the yāʾ a substitute for the nūn that is in insān. Insān may also be pluralized as insānīn, just as al-nashyān (one who is drunk or who investigates news) is pluralized as nashāyīn. (It is said: a man is nashwān, from intoxication; and nashyān for news means one who tests reports at the first time they arrive and searches for them. Its root is with a wāw.)

If it is said: anāsī is the plural whose singular is insī, so this is also a reported position: anāsī may be pluralized with a lightened yāʾ, and whoever pluralizes it this way seems to have dropped the yāʾ between the ʿayn and the lām of the verb, just as qarqūr is pluralized as qarāqīr and qarāqir. What supports their pluralizing it with the lightened form is the Arab saying: anāsiyya kathīra.

* *

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them that they might remember, but most people refused except ingratitude﴾ [25:50].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We have indeed apportioned this water which We sent down from the sky as pure, to give life thereby to the dead of the earth, among My servants, so that they might remember My blessings upon them and thank My favours toward them and My kindness to them. ﴿But most people refused except ingratitude﴾, meaning: they refused except to deny My blessings upon them and My favours upon them.

Those who are people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim relating to Ṭāwūs, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: No year is more abundant in rain than another, but Allah distributes it among His creation. He said: Then he recited: ﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them﴾.

- Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Sulaymān al-Taymī, who said: al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: No year is more abundant in rain than another, but He distributes it across the lands. Then he recited: ﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them that they might remember﴾.

- al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, regarding His words: ﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them﴾, he said: The rain He sends down upon one land and does not send down upon another land. He said: Then ʿIkrima said: ﴿We have distributed it among them that they might remember﴾.

- Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them that they might remember﴾: The rain falls once here and once there.

- Saʿīd ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Rāzī narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, that he heard Abū Juḥayfa say: I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd say: No year is more rainy than another, but He distributes it. Then ʿAbdullāh said: ﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them﴾.

As for His words: ﴿But most people refused except ingratitude﴾, al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrima: ﴿But most people refused except ingratitude﴾, he said: It is their saying about the anwāʾ (the rising and setting of stars, by which they attributed rain to them).

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water, that We may give life thereby to a dead land and give it to drink, of what We have created, cattle and many people﴾ [25:48–49].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And Allah is the One who sends the winds that fertilize (the clouds), ﴿as glad tidings﴾, meaning life, or from al-hayā' (rain-bringing) and the rain which He sends down upon His servants. ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾, meaning: We send down from the clouds, which We produced by the winds, above you, O people, pure water. ﴿That We may give life thereby to a dead land﴾, meaning a barren, parched land that produces nothing. He said ﴿a dead land﴾ and did not say "dead (feminine)," because by this He intends a dead place and locality. ﴿And give it to drink﴾ of what We have created, ﴿cattle﴾ among the beasts, ﴿and many people﴾. The word ﴿anāsī﴾ is the plural of insān (human), and its plural is anāsī. He made the yāʾ a substitute for the nūn that is in insān. Insān may also be pluralized as insānīn, just as al-nashyān (one who is drunk or who investigates news) is pluralized as nashāyīn. (It is said: a man is nashwān, from intoxication; and nashyān for news means one who tests reports at the first time they arrive and searches for them. Its root is with a wāw.)

If it is said: anāsī is the plural whose singular is insī, so this is also a reported position: anāsī may be pluralized with a lightened yāʾ, and whoever pluralizes it this way seems to have dropped the yāʾ between the ʿayn and the lām of the verb, just as qarqūr is pluralized as qarāqīr and qarāqir. What supports their pluralizing it with the lightened form is the Arab saying: anāsiyya kathīra.

* *

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them that they might remember, but most people refused except ingratitude﴾ [25:50].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We have indeed apportioned this water which We sent down from the sky as pure, to give life thereby to the dead of the earth, among My servants, so that they might remember My blessings upon them and thank My favours toward them and My kindness to them. ﴿But most people refused except ingratitude﴾, meaning: they refused except to deny My blessings upon them and My favours upon them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verses 51–52:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town. So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it, a great striving.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Had We willed, O Muhammad, We would have sent to every city and town a warner who would warn them of Our punishment for their disbelief in Us. Then much of the burden of what We have laden you with would be lightened, and a great hardship would be removed from you thereby. But We laden you with the weight of warning all the villages, so that by your patience in bearing it, if you are patient, you would merit what Allah has prepared for you of honour in His presence and the lofty ranks before Him. So do not obey the disbelievers in what they call you to, namely worshipping their gods, lest We make you taste double the life and double the death. Rather, strive against them with this Qur'an, a great striving, until they submit to acknowledging the obligations of Allah contained in it, and adopt it as their religion and comply with acting upon all of it, willingly or unwillingly.

Similar to what we have said regarding His saying, ﴿and strive against them with it﴾, is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying, ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it﴾: "With the Qur'an."

Others said regarding this, what follows:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, ﴿and strive against them with it, a great striving﴾: "It is Islam." And he recited ﴿And let them find in you harshness [ghilzah]﴾, and recited ﴿and be harsh upon them﴾, and said: "This is the great striving."

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who let loose the two seas, this one sweet, palatable, and that one salty, bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition﴾ (25:53)

He, the Exalted, says: And Allah is the One who mingled the two seas, so that one of them flows into the other and pours into it. The root of marij (مرج) is "mixing," and then "letting go" is also called marj, because when a man lets a thing go until it mixes with something else, it is as if he has mingled it. From this comes the report from the Prophet ﷺ and his saying to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr: "How will you be, ʿAbd Allah, when you are among the worthless remnant of people, whose covenants and trusts have become mixed up (marijat), and they become like this," and he interlaced his fingers. By his saying "marijat" he means: became mixed. From the same root is Allah's saying: ﴿in a confused matter﴾ (50:5), meaning mixed up. It is said that the pasture is called marj from this, because mixed kinds of animals graze in it. It is also said: "I let loose (marajtu) your animal," meaning I let it go wherever it wished. From the same root is the words of the rajaz poet:

"He grazed among them in a spring meadow, a pasture (mumarraj)." [[A line of rajaz verse by al-ʿAjjaj the rajaz poet (his Diwan, Leipzig edition of 1093, p. 9), being the eighty-second line of his poem that begins: "What stirred up sorrows and longing, has stirred..." Its editor vocalized the word mumarraj with a damma on the first mim and a kasra on the ra', but the correct form is as in Lisan al-ʿArab, which we have quoted from it; it is a noun of place from marraja al-dabba (of the form nasara) meaning he let his animal go to graze in the marj.]]

Those of the exegetical tradition said the same as what we have said about this:

Mentioned by those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿And it is He who let loose the two seas﴾: meaning, He made one of them slip over the other.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿let loose the two seas﴾: he poured one of them over the other.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿And it is He who let loose the two seas﴾: he says: He made one of them slip over the other.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Tumayla related to us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid: ﴿let loose﴾: he poured one of them over the other.

* *

And His words: ﴿this one sweet, palatable﴾

Al-furat: extremely sweet. It is said: "This is furat water," meaning extremely sweet. And His words: ﴿and that one salty, bitter﴾: he says: and this one is salty, bitter. By the sweet, palatable he means the waters of the rivers and rains, and by the salty, bitter he means the waters of the seas.

He only means by this that, from His blessing upon His creatures and the greatness of His dominion, He mixes the sweet water of the sea with the salty, bitter water of the sea, and then He prevents the salt from changing the sweet from its sweetness and corrupting it, by His decree and power, lest its corruption of it harm the travelers on both of them, so that they would find no water to drink when they are in need of water. So He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier﴾, meaning a partition that prevents each of them from corrupting the other. ﴿And an inviolable partition﴾: he says: and He made each of them a forbidden, prohibited thing for the other, that it should change or corrupt it.

Those of the exegetical tradition said the same as what we have said in interpreting this:

Mentioned by those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿this one sweet, palatable and that one salty, bitter﴾: meaning, He made one of them slip over the other, so the sweet does not corrupt the salty, nor does the salty corrupt the sweet. And His words: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier﴾: he said: the barrier is the land between them. ﴿And an inviolable partition﴾: meaning, one of them is partitioned off from the other by His command and decree; this is like His words: ﴿and placed between the two seas a barrier﴾ [27:61].

And Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier﴾: he said: a prison; His words: ﴿and an inviolable partition﴾: he said: the sea does not mix with the sweet.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier﴾: he said: a barrier that no one sees; the sweet does not mix in the sea. Ibn Jurayj said: I have not found a sweet sea except the sweet rivers, for the Tigris falls into the sea, and the expert informed me that it falls into the sea and does not surge in it; between them is like a white thread, and when it returns it does not return on its course from the sea; and the Nile pours into the sea.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Tumayla related to me, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier﴾: he said: the barrier is that they meet but do not mix; and His words: ﴿an inviolable partition﴾: meaning the saltiness of this does not mix with the sweetness of that; neither one transgresses against the other.

Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya related to us, from Rajaʾ, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition﴾: he said: this is dryness.

al-Hasan related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition﴾: he said: He made this one salty, bitter; he said: and the ajaj is bitter.

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say: ﴿let loose the two seas, this one sweet, palatable and that one salty, bitter﴾: he says: He made one of them slip over the other, so neither of them changes the taste of the other; ﴿and He placed between them a barrier﴾: it is the appointed term between this world and the Hereafter; ﴿and an inviolable partition﴾: Allah placed between the two seas a partition, that is, a barrier that holds one of them back from the other by His command and decree.

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: (and He placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition): and He placed between them a screen so that they do not meet. He said: When one of the Arabs speaks to another with something he dislikes, he says "hijran" (a partition), he said: a screen instead of what you say.

Abu Jaʿfar said: We have chosen the interpretation we have chosen for the meaning of His words: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition﴾ in preference to the view of those who said its meaning is that He placed between them a barrier of land or dryness, because the Exalted, in the beginning of the verse, informed that He let loose the two seas, and marj in the speech of the Arabs is mixing, as I explained earlier. Had the barrier between the sweet, palatable water and the salty, bitter one been land or dryness, there would be no letting loose of the two seas, yet He, may His praise be exalted, has informed us that He let them loose. We only recognize His power through His restraining this salty, bitter water from corrupting this sweet, palatable one, while each of them mixes with its companion. As for when each of them is in its own place apart from the other's place, there is no letting loose there, nor is there in it the wonder that people ignorant of it take note of and are reminded by, though everything our Lord originates is wondrous, and in it are the greatest lessons, admonitions, and conclusive proofs.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 54–55:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who created from water a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And your Lord is ever Competent.﴾ (54)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And Allah is the One who created from the sperm-drops a human being, a person, and made him [a relative by] lineage, which is seven [kinds], and [by] marriage, which is five."

As reported:

⁕ I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage﴾: "The lineage [kinship] is seven, [corresponding to] His words: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers...﴾ up to His words ﴿and the daughters of the sister﴾. And the marriage [relationship] is five, [corresponding to] His words: ﴿And your mothers who have nursed you...﴾ up to His words ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent.﴾

He says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is possessed of power to create whatever creation He wills, and to direct them as He wishes and intends.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship other than Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord.﴾ (55)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: The polytheists worship, besides Allah, gods that do not benefit them, bringing them any gain if they worship them, nor harm them if they abandon their worship, and they abandon the worship of the One who has bestowed upon them these blessings, the least of which none can match. These are what He, may His majesty be great, has enumerated to us in these verses, from His words: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow...﴾ up to His words: ﴿competent.﴾ And from His power is the power by which nothing He wills can be prevented from Him, and nothing He intends to do is impossible for Him. And when He wills to punish some of His servants who disobeyed Him, He brings upon them what He brought upon those whose description He gave: the people of Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of the Rass, and many generations between them. None of those against whom He is angry has a helper, nor does anything repel Him. ﴿And the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾. He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The disbeliever was an aide to Satan against his Lord, supporting him in disobedience to Him.

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾: "He backs Satan in disobeying Allah, precisely."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, who said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith told me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿against his Lord﴾: "Helping."

⁕ al-Qasim told us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same. Ibn Juraij said: Abu Jahl was a helper, backing Satan against his Lord.

⁕ al-Hasan told us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾: "An aide to Satan against his Lord in sins."

⁕ Yunus told me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾: "Against his Lord, a helper. And the ẓahīr (helper) is the ʿawīn (aide)." He recited the saying of Allah: ﴿So do not be an aide (ẓahīran) to the disbelievers﴾ and said: "Do not be an aide to them." He also recited the saying of Allah: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses﴾ and said: "Those who supported them: helped them."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, who said: My father told me, who said: My paternal uncle told me, who said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾: he means Abu al-Hakam, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Some of them gave the meaning of His words ﴿And the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾ a different direction: namely, "the disbeliever was contemptible to his Lord," from the Arabic saying: "I turned my back on him (ẓahartu bihi), so I did not pay attention to him," when one places him behind his back and does not turn to him. It was as though, in their view, ẓahīr was a fa'īl transformed from a maf'ūl, from "maẓhūr bihi" (one who is turned his back upon), as if it were said: "the disbeliever was one turned his back upon." But the view we have stated is the proper sense of the speech and the correct meaning, because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, reported the worship of these disbelievers besides Him, so it is more fitting that the speech follow this with His censure of them and censure of their action, rather than a report about their contemptibility before their Lord; and no mention had preceded of their arrogance toward Him, that it be followed by a report of their contemptibility before Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 54–55:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who created from water a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And your Lord is ever Competent.﴾ (54)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And Allah is the One who created from the sperm-drops a human being, a person, and made him [a relative by] lineage, which is seven [kinds], and [by] marriage, which is five."

As reported:

⁕ I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage﴾: "The lineage [kinship] is seven, [corresponding to] His words: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers...﴾ up to His words ﴿and the daughters of the sister﴾. And the marriage [relationship] is five, [corresponding to] His words: ﴿And your mothers who have nursed you...﴾ up to His words ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent.﴾

He says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is possessed of power to create whatever creation He wills, and to direct them as He wishes and intends.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship other than Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord.﴾ (55)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: The polytheists worship, besides Allah, gods that do not benefit them, bringing them any gain if they worship them, nor harm them if they abandon their worship, and they abandon the worship of the One who has bestowed upon them these blessings, the least of which none can match. These are what He, may His majesty be great, has enumerated to us in these verses, from His words: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow...﴾ up to His words: ﴿competent.﴾ And from His power is the power by which nothing He wills can be prevented from Him, and nothing He intends to do is impossible for Him. And when He wills to punish some of His servants who disobeyed Him, He brings upon them what He brought upon those whose description He gave: the people of Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of the Rass, and many generations between them. None of those against whom He is angry has a helper, nor does anything repel Him. ﴿And the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾. He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The disbeliever was an aide to Satan against his Lord, supporting him in disobedience to Him.

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾: "He backs Satan in disobeying Allah, precisely."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, who said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith told me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿against his Lord﴾: "Helping."

⁕ al-Qasim told us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same. Ibn Juraij said: Abu Jahl was a helper, backing Satan against his Lord.

⁕ al-Hasan told us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾: "An aide to Satan against his Lord in sins."

⁕ Yunus told me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And the disbeliever is ever an assistant [against] his Lord﴾: "Against his Lord, a helper. And the ẓahīr (helper) is the ʿawīn (aide)." He recited the saying of Allah: ﴿So do not be an aide (ẓahīran) to the disbelievers﴾ and said: "Do not be an aide to them." **The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿We have not sent you, [Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner (56). Say, "I do not ask you for any wage for it, except that whoever wills may take to his Lord a way (57)."﴾

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "We have not sent you," O Muhammad, to those to whom We sent you, "except as a bringer of good tidings" of a great reward for whoever believes in you and affirms you, and believes in what I have brought them from Me, and acts upon it, "and a warner" to whoever denies you and denies what I have brought them from Me, so that they do not affirm it and do not act upon it. "Say," to him: Say to these people to whom I have sent you, "I do not ask you, O people, for any wage for what I have brought you from my Lord," so that you would say: "Muhammad only seeks our wealth by what he calls us to, so we will not follow him in it, nor will we give him any of our wealth." "Except that whoever wills to take to his Lord a way" means: rather, whoever among you wills, let him take to his Lord a way, a path, by spending of his wealth in His cause, and in what brings him closer to Him, such as charity and expenditure in fighting His enemy, and other paths of goodness.

* *

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and glorify [Him] with His praise. And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants (58).﴾

His saying, exalted is He: And rely, O Muhammad, upon the One who has everlasting life, with no death after it. So trust in Him in the matter of your Lord, entrust yourself to Him, submit to Him, and be patient over what befalls you in it.

* *

His saying: ﴿"And glorify [Him] with His praise"﴾

That is: worship Him, giving thanks to Him for what He has bestowed upon you. His saying: ﴿"And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants"﴾ means: and the Ever-Living who does not die is sufficient for you as One who is aware of the sins of His creation, for nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He counts all of them against them until He recompenses them for them on the Day of Resurrection.
