[The verse is by Salamah ibn Jandal, as the author said. (See *al-Lisan*, root *a-w-b*.) *Al-muqamat* is the plural of *muqamah*, meaning *iqamah*. *Ta'wib* in the language of the Arabs means marching the whole day until night. He says: we pass our lives in this way: we make one day for dwelling, when the men of judgment among us gather in their assemblies to consult and to arrange the affairs of the tribe; and the other day we make for raiding the enemies, attacking them, and even if we march to them the whole day, we do not care, for we are people of might and protection. The author cited it at His words, describing Hell: ﴿indeed it is evil as a place of settling and a place of abode﴾, meaning a dwelling.]

And from *muqam* in the sense of a sitting place is the verse of 'Abbas ibn Mirdas:

"Whichever of us, you or I, was the worse, let him be led to the *maqamah* (assembly), not seeing it."

[The verse is by 'Abbas ibn Mirdas, which Ibn Barri cited in *al-Lisan* (root *q-w-m*), and it is evidence that *al-maqam* and *al-maqamah*, with a *fatha* on the *mim*, mean a sitting place. Al-Baghdadi said in *al-Khizanah* (2:230): he invokes curse upon whichever of them is the worse, meaning: whoever among us is worse, may God blind him in this world, so that he does not see until he is led to his assembly. The commentator on *al-Lubab* said: that is, he is led to the places where people stand and gather on the plains, not seeing them, i.e., a blind man who cannot see the assembly. The verse is one of several by 'Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami, which he composed for Khafaf ibn Nadbah concerning a dispute between them.]

He means: the assembly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 67:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but hold a balance between that﴾ [Qur'an 25:67]

His, the Exalted's, remembrance says: "And those who, when they spend their wealth, do not exceed in spending it."

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the expenditure that God meant in this place, and what extravagance (al-israf) and stinginess (al-iqtar) are in it. Some of them said: Extravagance is any expenditure in disobedience to God, even if it is little. He said: It is this that God meant, and He called it extravagance. They said: And stinginess is withholding what is due to God.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but hold a balance between that﴾ He said: They are the believers who are not extravagant, so they do not spend in disobedience to God, and who are not stingy, so they do not withhold the rights of God, the Exalted.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, who said: If you spent gold equal to Mount Abu Qubays in obedience to God, it would not be extravagance; and if you spent a sa' in disobedience to God, it would be extravagance.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾ He said: In spending on what He forbade them, even if it is a single dirham, and they are not stingy, nor do they fall short in spending on what is right.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but hold a balance between that﴾ He said: They are not extravagant by spending in disobedience to God; everything spent in disobedience to God, even if little, is extravagance; and they are not stingy by withholding from obedience to God. He said: Whatever is withheld from obedience to God, even if it is much, is stinginess.

He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Nushayt informed me, from Umar, client of Ghufra, that he was asked what extravagance is. He said: Everything you spend in other than obedience to God is extravagance.

Others said: Extravagance is exceeding the limit in spending, and stinginess is falling short of what is necessary.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, regarding His words: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾ He said: He does not leave them hungry, nor naked, and he does not spend an expenditure that people say is extravagant.

Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays Abu Abd Allah al-Makhzumi al-Makki narrated to us, he said: I heard Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, Abu al-Ward, client of Banu Makhzum, say: A scholar met a scholar who was above him in knowledge, and he said: May God have mercy on you, tell me about this building in which there is no extravagance, what is it? He said: It is what shelters you from the sun and covers you from the rain. He said: May God have mercy on you, tell me about this food whose portion has no extravagance, what is it? He said: What fends off hunger and falls short of satiety. He said: May God have mercy on you, tell me about this clothing in which there is no extravagance, what is it? He said: What covers your nakedness and warms you against the cold.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, concerning this verse: ﴿And those who, when they spend﴾ ... the verse. He said: They did not wear a garment for beauty, nor eat food for pleasure; rather, they sought from clothing what would cover their nakedness and shield them from heat and cold, and from food what would fend off hunger and strengthen them for worshipping their Lord.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from al-Ala ibn Abd al-Karim, from Yazid ibn Murra al-Ju'fi. He said: Knowledge is better than action, and the good deed lies between two evil deeds, meaning: when they spend, they are neither extravagant nor stingy, and the best of deeds are their middling ones.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Ka'b ibn Farrukh narrated to us, he said: Qatada narrated to us, from Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah, who said: The best of these matters are their middling ones, and the good deed lies between two evil deeds. I said to Qatada: What is "the good deed between two evil deeds"? He said: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾ ... the verse.

Others said: Extravagance is that you consume the property of another without right.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Salim ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Ma'dan, who said: I was with Awn ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba, and he said: The extravagant one is not he who consumes his own property; rather, the extravagant one is he who consumes the property of others.

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is the view of those who said: The extravagance in expenditure that God meant in this place is going beyond the limit that God has permitted to His servants to what lies above it; and stinginess is falling short of what God has commanded; and the balance (al-qawam) is between these.

We said this because the extravagant person and the stingy person are described as such; and if extravagance and stinginess in expenditure were permitted, neither would be blamed, and neither the extravagant nor the stingy would be blameworthy, because one whose action God has permitted does not deserve blame for it.

If someone says: Is there a known limit for this that you can make clear to us? It is said: Yes, this is understood in every matter of food, drink, clothing, charity, acts of righteousness and other things. We dislike lengthening the book by mentioning each kind in detail, but the sum of it is what we have explained. Such as a person eating food beyond satiety to the point that it weakens his body, exhausts his strength and distracts him from obeying his Lord and performing His obligations; that is from extravagance. And that he abstains from eating while he has access to it, until that weakens his body, exhausts his strength and makes him unable to perform the obligations of his Lord; that is from stinginess. Between these is the balance, in this manner, everything resembling what we have mentioned. As for taking a garment for beauty, which one wears when gathering with people, attending assemblies, gatherings and festivals, instead of his work garment, or eating food that strengthens him for worshipping his Lord, rising above what merely fends off hunger, of lesser foods, provided it does not aid the body beyond what is needed for standing in duty before God, that is outside the meaning of extravagance; rather, it is of the balance, because the Prophet ﷺ commanded some of that and encouraged some of it, as in his saying: "Is there anything wrong with one of you having two garments: a garment for his work and a garment for his Friday prayer and his festivals?" and his saying: "When God bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see its effect upon him," and what is similar to these reports which we have explained in their places.

As for His words: ﴿but hold a balance between that﴾, it is the expenditure with justice and kindness, as we have explained.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Sulayman, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding His words: ﴿and hold a balance between that﴾ He said: Half of their wealth.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿and hold a balance between that﴾: spending with right.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and hold a balance between that﴾ He said: The balance (al-qawam) is that they spend in obedience to God and withhold from the prohibitions of God.

He said: Ibrahim ibn Nushayt informed me, from Umar, client of Ghufra, who said: I asked him: What is al-qawam? He said: Al-qawam is that you do not spend in what is not right, nor withhold from what is your right to give. Al-qawam in the language of the Arabs, with a fatha on the qaf, means a thing between two things. You say of a woman of moderate build: indeed she has a fine qawam in her moderation, as al-Hutay'a said:

Umama circled among the riders at times... how fine is her qawam and her niqab.

[The line is by al-Hutay'a: "awana" is the plural of "awan." "Qawam" is the goodness of stature. "Muntaqab" is a mimetic verbal noun meaning "veiling." He says: Umama would at times circle among the riders, how moderate her stature and how fine her veiling. The niqab is the covering placed over the bridge of the nose of the face coverings, and the nuqba is the manner of wearing it; one says: so-and-so's nuqba is fine. The meaning of qawam is likewise: a thing midway between two things. The author applied this meaning to the line.]

As for when the qaf is kasra, and you say: He is the qiwam of his family, it means that by him their affair and their concern stand. There are other dialectal forms of it; one says of it: he is the qiyam of his family and their qayyim, in the sense of their qiwam. So the meaning of the passage is: their expenditure was between extravagance and stinginess, a moderate balance, neither exceeding the limit of God nor falling short of what God has obligated, but justice between these according to what He, the Mighty and Majestic, permitted, allowed and granted leave for.

The readers differed in the recitation of His words: ﴿وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾ The common readers of Medina recited it "وَلَمْ يُقْتِروا" with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the ta, from aqtara yuqtiru. The common readers of Kufa recited ﴿وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾ with a fatha on the ya and a damma on the ta, from qatara yaqturu. The common readers of Basra recited "وَلَمْ يَقْتِروا" with a fatha on the ya and a kasra on the ta, from qatara yaqtiru.

The correct view on this matter is that all these readings, despite the differences in their wording, are well-known dialects among the Arabs and widely transmitted recitations, and among the readers of the regions they have one meaning. So whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

We have already explained the meaning of extravagance and stinginess with their evidences from Arabic usage in our book on the language of the Arabs, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it in this place. As for the accusative of al-qawam, there are two possibilities: the first is what I mentioned, namely that the subject of kana is the expenditure, in the sense: "their expenditure, what they spent, was between that a balance," i.e., justice. The second is that bayn is the subject, so that although it is in the accusative in form, it is in the nominative in meaning, as one says: "kana dunahadha laka kafiyan," meaning: "less than this was sufficient for you." Likewise in His words: ﴿وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَامًا﴾, because its meaning is: "and the middle of that was a balance."

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that will meet a penalty.﴾ (25:68) ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾ (25:69) ﴿Except for one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (25:70) ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work — indeed, he turns to Allah with a [sincere] return.﴾ (25:71)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Those who do not worship another god alongside Allah, so that they associate others in their worship of Him, but rather they devote worship sincerely to Him and single Him out for obedience. ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾ to be killed, ﴿except by right﴾, that is, either for disbelief in Allah after having embraced Islam, or for adultery after having been married (muhsan), or for killing a soul, in which case it is killed in retribution. ﴿And do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, that is, they do not commit what Allah has forbidden them to commit of intimacy with forbidden private parts. ﴿And whoever does that﴾ means: whoever commits these acts, invoking another god alongside Allah, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden without right, and committing adultery. ﴿Will meet a penalty﴾ means: he will meet a punishment and retribution from Allah's chastisement, as our Lord, may His praise be exalted, described it: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾

And among the meanings of ʾithām (penalty) is the saying of Bal'a' ibn Qays al-Kinani:

*"May Allah reward Ibn ʿUrwa, since he has become [one who commits] disobedience to parents, and disobedience to parents brings a penalty (ithām) for him."*

[[The verse is attributed to Bal'a' ibn Qays ibn Rabi'a ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yaʿmur, whose name is Ḥumayḍa, and he is of Kinana ibn Khuzayma. Bal'a' was the chief of the Banu Kinana in most of their wars and expeditions, and he conducted many raids against the Arabs, and he has reports concerning the wars of al-Fijar. He was a skilled poet who composed good poetry in every genre (see al-Mu'talif wa'l-Mukhtalif, p. 106, and Mu'jam al-Shu'ara' of al-Marzubani, p. 357). The verse was recited by the author of Lisan al-Arab (under "athama") and he attributed it to Shafiʿ al-Laythi. Abu ʿUbayda, in Majaz al-Qur'an, attributed it to Bal'a' ibn Qays al-Kinani, and the author [al-Tabari] took from him. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab: "Abu Ishaq said: the interpretation of ithām is recompense. Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani said: 'So-and-so met the ithām of that,' i.e., the recompense of that, for al-Khalil and Sibawayh went to the view that its meaning is: he will meet the recompense of the ithām. And the saying of Shafiʿ al-Laythi on this: 'May Allah reward Ibn ʿUrwa ... ... ... disobedience to parents, and it brings a penalty for him.'"]]

That is, the penalty for the act of disobeying parents, which is severing ties of kinship. Al-Layth said: "In the general sense of the exegesis, ithām means the penalty of sin." It has also been said regarding His words ﴿will meet a penalty﴾: it is a valley in Hell. Ibn Sayyida said: "The correct view in my opinion is that its meaning is: he will meet the punishment of ithām." End quote.

By ithām is meant: punishment.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a group of polytheists who wished to enter Islam, and who had committed these sins in their polytheism. They feared that Islam would not benefit them because of what had passed from them of such things, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, and Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed this verse, informing them that Allah accepts the repentance of whoever of them repents.

Those who said this:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Yaʿla ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that some people from among the polytheists had killed a great deal, so they came to Muhammad ﷺ and said: "What you call us to is indeed good; if only you would tell us that there is an expiation for what we have done!" So there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ up to His words: ﴿before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾ (39:53–55). Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said the same as the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, exactly.

- ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Muʿawiya, from Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ: "What are the major sins?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you; that you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you; and that you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to us from the Book of Allah: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash and Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from ʿAmr ibn Sharahbil, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you make a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." So there was revealed, confirming the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ ... the verse.

- Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar narrated to us, he said: ʿAli ibn Qadim narrated to us, he said: Asbat ibn Nasr al-Hamdani narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from Abu Maysara, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.

- ʿIsa ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿIsa al-Ramli narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle Yahya ibn ʿIsa narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, from Sufyan, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" Then he mentioned something similar.

- Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to me, he said: ʿAmir ibn Mudrik narrated to us, he said: al-Sarri — meaning Ibn Ismaʿil — narrated to us, he said: al-Shaʿbi narrated to us, from Masruq, who said: ʿAbd Allah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day, and I followed him. He sat on a raised piece of ground, and I sat beneath him, my face facing his knees. I seized the opportunity of his solitude and said: 'May my father and mother be ransom for you, O Messenger of Allah, which sins are greatest?' He said: 'That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you.' I said: 'Then what?' He said: 'That you kill your child out of fear that he will eat with you.' I said: 'Then what?' He said: 'That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour.' Then he recited this verse: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ ... to the end of the verse."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, from Za'ida, from Mansur, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated to me — or I was told from Saʿid ibn Jubayr — that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abza ordered him to ask Ibn ʿAbbas about the two verses: the one in al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ ... to the end of the verse, and the verse in al-Furqan: ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ up to ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "If a man enters Islam, learns its laws and its commands, and then kills a believer intentionally, there is no repentance for him. As for the verse in al-Furqan, when it was revealed, the polytheists of Mecca said: 'We have indeed set up equals with Allah, and we have killed the soul which Allah has forbidden without right; so what benefit is Islam to us?'" He said: "Then there was revealed: ﴿except one who repents﴾." He said: "Whoever of them repents, it is accepted from him."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated to me — or he said: al-Hakam narrated to me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abza commanded me, saying: "Ask Ibn ʿAbbas about these two verses: what is the difference between the verse in al-Furqan, ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾ ... the verse, and the verse in al-Nisa', ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾." So I asked Ibn ʿAbbas about that, and he said: "When Allah revealed the one in al-Furqan, the polytheists of Mecca said: 'We have killed the soul which Allah has forbidden, and we have invoked another deity along with Allah.' So He said: ﴿except one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾ ... the verse. So that one is for those." As for the one in al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ ... the verse, that is when a man has known Islam, then kills a believer intentionally; his recompense is Hell, and there is no repentance for him." I mentioned that to Mujahid, and he said: "Except one who repents."

- Muhammad ibn ʿAwf al-Ta'i narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Dhuhli narrated to us, he said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Mansur ibn al-Muʿtamir, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated to me, who said: Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abza said to me: "Ask Ibn ʿAbbas about these two verses concerning the word of Allah: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ ... to ﴿except one who repents﴾, and concerning His word: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ ... to the end of the verse." He said: "So I asked Ibn ʿAbbas about them, and he said: 'This verse was revealed in al-Furqan in Mecca, up to His words: ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾ The polytheists said: "What benefit is Islam to us, when we have set up equals with Allah, killed the soul which Allah has forbidden, and committed indecencies?" So Allah revealed: ﴿except one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾ ... to the end of the verse.'" He said: "As for one who enters Islam and understands it, then kills, there is no repentance for him."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Abu Bishr, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said concerning this verse: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right﴾ ... the verse: "It was revealed concerning the people of polytheism."

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abza commanded me to ask Ibn ʿAbbas about this verse: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ ... and he mentioned something similar.

- ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿUmayr narrated to me, he said: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa ibn Shuʿayb ibn Thawban, a client of the Banu al-Dil from the people of Medina, narrated to us, from Fulayh al-Shammas, from ʿUbayd ibn Abi ʿUbayd, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the ʿatama [the night prayer], then I left, and there was a woman at my door. I greeted her, and she opened and entered. While I was in my mosque praying, she knocked at the door, so I gave her permission, and she entered and said: 'I have come to you to ask you about a deed I did; is there any repentance for me? I committed adultery and bore a child, then I killed him.' I said: 'No! What a bad eye! No honour!' Then she stood up, calling out in regret, saying: 'Alas! Was this beautiful child created for the Fire?' He said: 'Then I prayed the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from that night, then we sat waiting for permission to see him. He gave us permission, and we entered. Then those who were with me left, and I stayed behind. He said: "What is wrong with you, O Abu Hurayra? Do you have a need?" I said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, I prayed with you last night, then I left, and I related to him what the woman had said." The Prophet ﷺ said: "What did you say to her?" He said: "I said to her: 'No, by Allah! What a bad eye! No honour!'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Evil is what you said. Did you not read this verse: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right﴾ ... the verse, ﴿except one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾?" Then Abu Hurayra said: "So I went out and did not leave any fortress or house in Medina without standing before it. I said: 'If the woman who came to Abu Hurayra last night is among you, let her come to me and be given good news.' When I had prayed the evening prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, she was at my door. I said: 'Rejoice, for I entered upon the Prophet, and I mentioned to him what I said to you and what you said to me.' He said: 'Evil is what you said to her. Did you not read this verse?' I recited it to her, and she fell down prostrating, and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out and a repentance for what I did. Indeed, this girl and her son are freed for the sake of Allah's face, and I have repented of what I did.'"

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', who said: "I frequented Ibn ʿAbbas for thirteen years, and there was no part of the Qur'an except that I asked him about it, and my messenger frequented ʿA'isha. I neither heard him nor heard anyone of the scholars say: 'Allah says to a sin: I will not forgive it.'"

Others said: This verse is abrogated (mansukha) by the one in al-Nisa'.

Those who said this:

- Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: al-Mughira ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Harrani informed me, from Abu al-Zinad, from Kharija ibn Zayd, that he entered upon his father, and with him was a man from the people of Iraq, who was asking him about this verse in Tabaraka al-Furqan and the verse in al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾. Zayd ibn Thabit said: "You have known the abrogating from the abrogated. The one in al-Nisa' abrogated it, six months after it."

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: "This surah and [the verse] in al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾, are eight years apart." Ibn Jurayj said: "al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza informed me that he asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr: 'Is there repentance for one who kills a believer intentionally?' He said: 'No.' Then he recited to him this whole verse. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: 'I recited it to Ibn ʿAbbas just as you recited it to me, and he said: "This is Meccan; it was abrogated by a Medinan verse, the one in Surat al-Nisa'."' We have already set out the clarification of the correct view on this verse in Surat al-Nisa' with what makes its repetition here unnecessary."

In agreement with what we have said about the meaning of ithām, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said, except that they said: that is a punishment with which Allah punishes whoever commits these major sins, in a valley in Hell called Athām.

Those who said this:

- Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, he said: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrate, from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "Ithām is a valley in Hell."

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's word: ﴿will meet a penalty (athām)﴾, who said: "A valley in Hell."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid — Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrima, concerning His word: ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾, who said: "A valley in Hell in which are the adulterers."

- al-ʿAbbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, he said: Sharqi ibn Qutami narrated to us, from Luqman ibn ʿAmir al-Khuza'i, who said: "I came to Abu Umama Suday ibn ʿAjlan al-Bahili and said: 'Narrate to me a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' He ordered food for me, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'If a rock the weight of ten 'ashrawat were hurled from the edge of Hell, it would not reach its bottom in fifty autumns; then it would reach Ghayy and Athām.'" I said: "And what are Ghayy and Athām?" He said: "Two wells at the bottom of Hell, in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows. They are the two that Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿They neglected prayer and followed desires, so they will meet Ghayy﴾ (19:59), and His word in al-Furqan: ﴿And they do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse; and whoever does that will meet a penalty (athām)﴾."

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His word: ﴿will meet a penalty (athām)﴾: "Athām is evil." And he said: "What lies beyond that will suffice you: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾"

- al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His word: ﴿will meet a penalty (athām)﴾, who said: "Retribution (nakal)." He said: "And he said: it is a valley in Hell."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 68–71 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Hushaym, who said: Zakariyya ibn Abi Maryam informed us, saying: I heard Abu Umama al-Bahili say: "The distance between the brink of Jahannam and its bottom is seventy autumns' journey for a stone that falls into it, or a rock that plunges, whose size is like ten great well-fed camels' loads." A man said to him: "Is there anything beneath that?" He said: "Yes, Ghayy and Athām."
* *
His saying: ﴿Punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾

The reciters differed in its recitation. The common reciters of the cities, except ʿĀṣim, read ﴿yudāʿaf﴾ in the jussive (yuḍāʿafْ) and ﴿wa-yakhlud﴾ in the jussive. ʿĀṣim read ﴿yuḍāʿafu﴾ in the nominative and ﴿wa-yakhludu﴾ in the nominative, both as a new sentence (ibtidāʾ), holding that the speech ends at ﴿yalqa athāman﴾, and then begins with ﴿yuḍāʿafu lahu al-ʿadhāb﴾. The correct reading in our view is the jussive for both verbs: yuḍāʿaf and yakhlud. This is because it is an explanation (tafsīr) of athām and not a verb of its own; if it were a verb governed by what precedes, the proper form would be the nominative, as the poet said:

*mattā ta'tihi ta'shū ilā ḍawʾi nārihi... tajid khayra nārin ʿindahā khayru mūqidi*

[This verse is by al-Ḥuṭayʾa (Lisan: ʿashā). He said: ʿashā ilā al-nār, and ʿashāhā ʿashwan and ʿushwan (like faʿūl), and iʿtashāhā and iʿtashā bihā, all meaning: he saw it at night from a distance, so he headed toward it seeking its light. al-Ḥuṭayʾa said: "Whenever you come to him..." i.e., whenever you come to him, you cannot make out his fire because of your weak sight. End of quote. The clause "ta'shū" is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). That is why the author said: "ta'shū is nominative because it is a verb governed by ta'tihi," i.e., it is a circumstantial clause of the subject of ta'tihi: "whenever you come to him walking blindly."]

As for what al-Tabari transmitted, that the reciters differ over reading ﴿yuḍāʿaf﴾ in the jussive or the nominative, it is a sound statement, and each reading has its grammatical interpretation. However, he prefers the jussive reading as an explanation (tafsīr), i.e., a substitute (badal) for what precedes it, namely ﴿yalqa﴾. The view adopted by the author follows al-Farrāʾ in his *Maʿānī al-Qurʾān* (University of Jordan microfilm no. 24059, p. 226), who said: "As for his saying: ﴿Whoever does that will meet athām; punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾, the reciters read ﴿yuḍāʿaf﴾ in the jussive, while ʿĀṣim ibn Abi al-Najūd read it in the nominative; the correct form is the jussive. If you explain it and it is not a verb governed by what precedes it (i.e., accompanying the verb before it), then the correct form is the jussive. If it is a verb governed by what precedes it, you use the nominative. As for what explains the jussive (i.e., what is substituted for it), it is His saying: ﴿Whoever does that will meet athām﴾, then He explained athām by saying ﴿punishment will be doubled for him﴾. A similar example in speech is: 'If you speak to me, advising me toward goodness and righteousness, I will accept from you.' Do you not see that you explained the speech as 'righteousness,' and it was not a verb of the first, so you used the jussive? If the second were a verb of the first, you would use the nominative, as in your saying: 'If you come to us seeking good, you will find it.' Do you not see that 'tajid' and 'taṭlub' are verbs of 'come,' as in your saying: 'If you come to us seeking good, you will find it'? The poet said: 'Whenever you come to him...' — so he used the nominative of ta'shū because he meant: 'whenever you come to him walking blindly.' ʿĀṣim read ﴿yuḍāʿafu lahu﴾ in the nominative because he intended a new sentence (istiʾnāf), as you say: 'If you come to us, we will honor you, giving you all you desire,' not as a conditional."

So ta'shū is nominative because it is a verb governed by ta'tihi, meaning: "whenever you come to him walking blindly."

* *
His saying ﴿And he will abide therein in humiliation﴾

He will remain in it forever, without end, in disgrace. His saying: ﴿Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work﴾: the Exalted says: whoever does these deeds He has mentioned will meet athām, ﴿except one who repents﴾, meaning: except one who returns to obedience to Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, by abandoning that and turning toward what Allah is pleased with, ﴿and believes﴾, meaning: and affirms what Muhammad, the Prophet of Allah, brought, ﴿and does righteous work﴾, meaning: and acts upon what Allah has commanded him of deeds and refrains from what Allah has forbidden.

* *
His saying: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) differed concerning its meaning. Some said: its meaning is: Allah will replace the ugly deeds they did in shirk with the fine deeds of Islam, replacing shirk with faith, the acts of the people of polytheism with the acts of the people of faith, and adultery with chastity and marriage.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abu Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾: he said: "They are believers who, before their faith, were upon evil deeds; Allah turned them away from that and transformed them to good deeds, substituting good deeds for their evil deeds."

⁕ Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work﴾ ... to the end of the verse, he said: "They are those who repent and then act in obedience, so Allah changes their evil deeds into good deeds when they repent."

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, from Saʿid, who said: It was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ ... to the end of the verse, concerning Waḥshī and his companions. They said: "How can we repent, when we worshipped idols, killed believers, and married polytheist women?" So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work — those Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾. Allah replaced their worship of idols with the worship of Allah, replaced their fighting alongside polytheists with fighting alongside Muslims against polytheists, and replaced marriage to polytheist women with marriage to believing women.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾, said: "Shirk into faith, killing into restraint, and adultery into chastity."

⁕ I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ — this verse is Meccan, revealed in Mecca — ﴿And whoever does that﴾, meaning: shirk, killing, and adultery all together. When Allah revealed this verse, the polytheists of Mecca said: "Muhammad claims that whoever commits shirk, kills, and commits adultery will have the Fire, and has no good with Allah." So Allah revealed ﴿except one who repents﴾ from among the polytheists of Mecca, ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾, meaning: Allah will replace shirk, killing, and adultery with faith in Allah and entry into Islam, and this is the change in this world. Allah also revealed concerning this: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins﴾, meaning by it what was in shirk; Allah says to them: ﴿Turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him﴾, calling them to Islam. These two verses are Meccan, while the verse in Surat al-Nisāʾ: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ ... the verse, is Madani, revealed in Medina, and between it and the one revealed in al-Furqan are eight years, and it is ambiguous with no way out.

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, saying: Abu Ḥamza narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas was asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾, and he said:

*Budditna baʿda ḥarrihi kharīfā... wa baʿda ṭūli al-nafasi al-wajīfā*

[This is a verse by Labid al-ʿAmiri the poet. This version is obscure. I did not find it in the original of his diwan, but in the appendix to the diwan (Leiden edition p. 56), and its version there is like al-Suyuti's in al-Itqan. That version is better and clearer: *Baddalna baʿda al-nafash al-wajīfā... wa baʿda ṭūli al-ḥirrati al-ṣarīfā*. Labid describes a group of camels that used to graze at night for a long time, then were changed from that swift pace (wajīf), a kind of rapid march of camels and horses; one says: the camel and the horse hastened, wajfan and wajīfan. They were changed after long chewing the cud in their resting places (al-ṣarīf). "Ijtirāʾ" means that the ruminant brings back part of its food to chew it well, then swallows it again. "Ṣarīf" has several meanings, including milk at the time of milking and wine; here it means the sound of the camel's teeth when moved, which happens when it is exhausted and weary. Labid seems to say that their conditions changed after comfort into misery.]

⁕ Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation﴾. The polytheists said: "By Allah, these people with Muhammad were only with us." He said: So Allah revealed ﴿except one who repents and believes﴾. He said: "Repented from shirk," and "believes in the punishment of Allah and His Messenger," ﴿and does righteous work﴾: he said: "affirms," ﴿those Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾. He said: Allah changes their evil deeds that were in shirk into righteous deeds when they entered faith.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: those Allah changes their evil deeds in this world into good deeds for them on the Day of Resurrection.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr al-Basri related to me, saying: Quraysh ibn Anas Abu Anas narrated to us, saying: Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum related to me, from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾: he said: "Their evil deeds will become good deeds for them on the Day of Resurrection."

⁕ al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafa narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ḥazim Abu Muʿawiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Maʿrur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I know the last of the people of the Fire to leave the Fire, and the last of the people of the Fire to enter Paradise. A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: 'Set aside his major sins and question him about his minor ones.' It will be said to him: 'You did such and such, and you did such and such.' He will say: 'O Lord, I did things that I do not see here.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molar teeth showed. It will be said to him: 'For you, in place of every evil deed, is a good deed.'"

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two interpretations is the view of one who interprets: "Allah will change their evil deeds," i.e., their deeds in shirk, into good deeds in Islam, by transferring them from what angers Allah to what pleases Him.

We said this is the more fitting interpretation of the verse because the evil deeds had already passed in their ugliness, and it is not possible to transform a thing that has passed with a certain attribute into a different state except by changing it from its previous attribute in another state. Thus, if this were done, the shirk of the disbeliever, which was shirk in its very essence, would have to become faith on the Day of Resurrection through Islam, and all his sins in their very essence would become obedience; and no person of sound reason would say that.

* *
His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾

The Exalted says: Allah is One who pardons the sins of whoever of His servants repents and returns to His obedience, and One who is merciful to him, not punishing him for his sins after he has repented from them.

* *
His saying: ﴿And whoever repents﴾

He says: whoever of the polytheists repents, believes in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and does righteous work﴾, meaning: acts upon what Allah commanded and obeys Him. Then Allah will do with him what He did with the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who repented, believed, and did righteous work before this verse was revealed: replacing his evil deeds in shirk with their goodness in Islam.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work, indeed he turns to Allah in repentance﴾: "This is for the polytheists who said, when ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ ... to His saying ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ was revealed, concerning the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'These were only with us.'" He said: "Whoever repents and does righteous work, for them is like what is for these ones: ﴿indeed he turns to Allah in repentance﴾ — repentance has not been forbidden to you."

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that will meet a penalty.﴾ (25:68) ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾ (25:69) ﴿Except for one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (25:70) ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work — indeed, he turns to Allah with a [sincere] return.﴾ (25:71)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Those who do not worship another god alongside Allah, so that they associate others in their worship of Him, but rather they devote worship sincerely to Him and single Him out for obedience. ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾ to be killed, ﴿except by right﴾, that is, either for disbelief in Allah after having embraced Islam, or for adultery after having been married (muhsan), or for killing a soul, in which case it is killed in retribution. ﴿And do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, that is, they do not commit what Allah has forbidden them to commit of intimacy with forbidden private parts. ﴿And whoever does that﴾ means: whoever commits these acts, invoking another god alongside Allah, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden without right, and committing adultery. ﴿Will meet a penalty﴾ means: he will meet a punishment and retribution from Allah's chastisement, as our Lord, may His praise be exalted, described it: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾

And among the meanings of ʾithām (penalty) is the saying of Bal'a' ibn Qays al-Kinani:

*"May Allah reward Ibn ʿUrwa, since he has become [one who commits] disobedience to parents, and disobedience to parents brings a penalty (ithām) for him."*

[[The verse is attributed to Bal'a' ibn Qays ibn Rabi'a ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yaʿmur, whose name is Ḥumayḍa, and he is of Kinana ibn Khuzayma. Bal'a' was the chief of the Banu Kinana in most of their wars and expeditions, and he conducted many raids against the Arabs, and he has reports concerning the wars of al-Fijar. He was a skilled poet who composed good poetry in every genre (see al-Mu'talif wa'l-Mukhtalif, p. 106, and Mu'jam al-Shu'ara' of al-Marzubani, p. 357). The verse was recited by the author of Lisan al-Arab (under "athama") and he attributed it to Shafiʿ al-Laythi. Abu ʿUbayda, in Majaz al-Qur'an, attributed it to Bal'a' ibn Qays al-Kinani, and the author [al-Tabari] took from him. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab: "Abu Ishaq said: the interpretation of ithām is recompense. Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani said: 'So-and-so met the ithām of that,' i.e., the recompense of that, for al-Khalil and Sibawayh went to the view that its meaning is: he will meet the recompense of the ithām. And the saying of Shafiʿ al-Laythi on this: 'May Allah reward Ibn ʿUrwa ... ... ... disobedience to parents, and it brings a penalty for him.'"]]

That is, the penalty for the act of disobeying parents, which is severing ties of kinship. Al-Layth said: "In the general sense of the exegesis, ithām means the penalty of sin." It has also been said regarding His words ﴿will meet a penalty﴾: it is a valley in Hell. Ibn Sayyida said: "The correct view in my opinion is that its meaning is: he will meet the punishment of ithām." End quote.

By ithām is meant: punishment.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a group of polytheists who wished to enter Islam, and who had committed these sins in their polytheism. They feared that Islam would not benefit them because of what had passed from them of such things, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, and Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed this verse, informing them that Allah accepts the repentance of whoever of them repents.

Those who said this:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Yaʿla ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that some people from among the polytheists had killed a great deal, so they came to Muhammad ﷺ and said: "What you call us to is indeed good; if only you would tell us that there is an expiation for what we have done!" So there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ up to His words: ﴿before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾ (39:53–55). Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said the same as the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, exactly.

- ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Muʿawiya, from Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ: "What are the major sins?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you; that you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you; and that you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." So there was revealed, confirming the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ ... the verse.

I mentioned that to Mujahid, and he said: "Except one who repents."

I greeted her, and she opened and entered. While I was in my mosque praying, she knocked at the door, so I gave her permission, and she entered and said: 'I have come to you to ask you about a deed I did; is there any repentance for me? I committed adultery and bore a child, then I killed him.' I said: 'No! What a bad eye! No honour!' Then she stood up, calling out in regret, saying: 'Alas! Was this beautiful child created for the Fire?' He said: 'Then I prayed the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from that night, then we sat waiting for permission to see him. He gave us permission, and we entered. Then those who were with me left, and I stayed behind. He said: "What is wrong with you, O Abu Hurayra? Do you have a need?" I said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, I prayed with you last night, then I left, and I related to him what the woman had said." The Prophet ﷺ said: "What did you say to her?" He said: "I said to her: 'No, by Allah! What a bad eye! No honour!'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Evil is what you said. Did you not read this verse: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right﴾ ... the verse, ﴿except one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾?" Then Abu Hurayra said: "So I went out and did not leave any fortress or house in Medina without standing before it. I said: 'If the woman who came to Abu Hurayra last night is among you, let her come to me and be given good news.' When I had prayed the evening prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, she was at my door. I said: 'Rejoice, for I entered upon the Prophet, and I mentioned to him what I said to you and what you said to me.' He said: 'Evil is what you said to her. Did you not read this verse?' I recited it to her, and she fell down prostrating, and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out and a repentance for what I did. Indeed, this girl and her son are freed for the sake of Allah's face, and I have repented of what I did.'"

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', who said: "I frequented Ibn ʿAbbas for thirteen years, and there was no part of the Qur'an except that I asked him about it, and my messenger frequented ʿA'isha. I neither heard him nor heard anyone of the scholars say: 'Allah says to a sin: I will not forgive it.'"

Others said: This verse is abrogated (mansukha) by the one in al-Nisa'.

Those who said this:

- Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: al-Mughira ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Harrani informed me, from Abu al-Zinad, from Kharija ibn Zayd, that he entered upon his father, and with him was a man from the people of Iraq, who was asking him about this verse in Tabaraka al-Furqan and the verse in al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾. Zayd ibn Thabit said: "You have known the abrogating from the abrogated. The one in al-Nisa' abrogated it, six months after it."

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: "This surah and [the verse] in al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾, are eight years apart." Ibn Jurayj said: "al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza informed me that he asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr: 'Is there repentance for one who kills a believer intentionally?' He said: 'No.' Then he recited to him this whole verse. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: 'I recited it to Ibn ʿAbbas just as you recited it to me, and he said: "This is Meccan; it was abrogated by a Medinan verse, the one in Surat al-Nisa'."' We have already set out the clarification of the correct view on this verse in Surat al-Nisa' with what makes its repetition here unnecessary."

In agreement with what we have said about the meaning of ithām, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said, except that they said: that is a punishment with which Allah punishes whoever commits these major sins, in a valley in Hell called Athām.

Those who said this:

- Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, he said: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrate, from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "Ithām is a valley in Hell."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid — Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrima, concerning His word: ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾, who said: "A valley in Hell in which are the adulterers."

He ordered food for me, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'If a rock the weight of ten 'ashrawat were hurled from the edge of Hell, it would not reach its bottom in fifty autumns; then it would reach Ghayy and Athām.'" I said: "And what are Ghayy and Athām?" He said: "Two wells at the bottom of Hell, in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows. They are the two that Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿They neglected prayer and followed desires, so they will meet Ghayy﴾ (19:59), and His word in al-Furqan: ﴿And they do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse; and whoever does that will meet a penalty (athām)﴾."

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His word: ﴿will meet a penalty (athām)﴾: "Athām is evil." And he said: "What lies beyond that will suffice you: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 68–71 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Hushaym, who said: Zakariyya ibn Abi Maryam informed us, saying: I heard Abu Umama al-Bahili say: "The distance between the brink of Jahannam and its bottom is seventy autumns' journey for a stone that falls into it, or a rock that plunges, whose size is like ten great well-fed camels' loads." A man said to him: "Is there anything beneath that?" He said: "Yes, Ghayy and Athām."
* *
His saying: ﴿Punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾

The reciters differed in its recitation. The common reciters of the cities, except ʿĀṣim, read ﴿yudāʿaf﴾ in the jussive (yuḍāʿafْ) and ﴿wa-yakhlud﴾ in the jussive. ʿĀṣim read ﴿yuḍāʿafu﴾ in the nominative and ﴿wa-yakhludu﴾ in the nominative, both as a new sentence (ibtidāʾ), holding that the speech ends at ﴿yalqa athāman﴾, and then begins with ﴿yuḍāʿafu lahu al-ʿadhāb﴾. The correct reading in our view is the jussive for both verbs: yuḍāʿaf and yakhlud. This is because it is an explanation (tafsīr) of athām and not a verb of its own; if it were a verb governed by what precedes, the proper form would be the nominative, as the poet said:

*mattā ta'tihi ta'shū ilā ḍawʾi nārihi... tajid khayra nārin ʿindahā khayru mūqidi*

[This verse is by al-Ḥuṭayʾa (Lisan: ʿashā). He said: ʿashā ilā al-nār, and ʿashāhā ʿashwan and ʿushwan (like faʿūl), and iʿtashāhā and iʿtashā bihā, all meaning: he saw it at night from a distance, so he headed toward it seeking its light. al-Ḥuṭayʾa said: "Whenever you come to him..." i.e., whenever you come to him, you cannot make out his fire because of your weak sight. End of quote. The clause "ta'shū" is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). That is why the author said: "ta'shū is nominative because it is a verb governed by ta'tihi," i.e., it is a circumstantial clause of the subject of ta'tihi: "whenever you come to him walking blindly."]

As for what al-Tabari transmitted, that the reciters differ over reading ﴿yuḍāʿaf﴾ in the jussive or the nominative, it is a sound statement, and each reading has its grammatical interpretation. However, he prefers the jussive reading as an explanation (tafsīr), i.e., a substitute (badal) for what precedes it, namely ﴿yalqa﴾. The view adopted by the author follows al-Farrāʾ in his *Maʿānī al-Qurʾān* (University of Jordan microfilm no. 24059, p. 226), who said: "As for his saying: ﴿Whoever does that will meet athām; punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾, the reciters read ﴿yuḍāʿaf﴾ in the jussive, while ʿĀṣim ibn Abi al-Najūd read it in the nominative; the correct form is the jussive. If you explain it and it is not a verb governed by what precedes it (i.e., accompanying the verb before it), then the correct form is the jussive. If it is a verb governed by what precedes it, you use the nominative. As for what explains the jussive (i.e., what is substituted for it), it is His saying: ﴿Whoever does that will meet athām﴾, then He explained athām by saying ﴿punishment will be doubled for him﴾. A similar example in speech is: 'If you speak to me, advising me toward goodness and righteousness, I will accept from you.' Do you not see that you explained the speech as 'righteousness,' and it was not a verb of the first, so you used the jussive? If the second were a verb of the first, you would use the nominative, as in your saying: 'If you come to us seeking good, you will find it.' Do you not see that 'tajid' and 'taṭlub' are verbs of 'come,' as in your saying: 'If you come to us seeking good, you will find it'? The poet said: 'Whenever you come to him...' — so he used the nominative of ta'shū because he meant: 'whenever you come to him walking blindly.' ʿĀṣim read ﴿yuḍāʿafu lahu﴾ in the nominative because he intended a new sentence (istiʾnāf), as you say: 'If you come to us, we will honor you, giving you all you desire,' not as a conditional."

So ta'shū is nominative because it is a verb governed by ta'tihi, meaning: "whenever you come to him walking blindly."

* *
His saying ﴿And he will abide therein in humiliation﴾

He will remain in it forever, without end, in disgrace. His saying: ﴿Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work﴾: the Exalted says: whoever does these deeds He has mentioned will meet athām, ﴿except one who repents﴾, meaning: except one who returns to obedience to Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, by abandoning that and turning toward what Allah is pleased with, ﴿and believes﴾, meaning: and affirms what Muhammad, the Prophet of Allah, brought, ﴿and does righteous work﴾, meaning: and acts upon what Allah has commanded him of deeds and refrains from what Allah has forbidden.

* *
His saying: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) differed concerning its meaning. Some said: its meaning is: Allah will replace the ugly deeds they did in shirk with the fine deeds of Islam, replacing shirk with faith, the acts of the people of polytheism with the acts of the people of faith, and adultery with chastity and marriage.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abu Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾: he said: "They are believers who, before their faith, were upon evil deeds; Allah turned them away from that and transformed them to good deeds, substituting good deeds for their evil deeds."

⁕ Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work﴾ ... to the end of the verse, he said: "They are those who repent and then act in obedience, so Allah changes their evil deeds into good deeds when they repent."

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, from Saʿid, who said: It was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ ... to the end of the verse, concerning Waḥshī and his companions. They said: "How can we repent, when we worshipped idols, killed believers, and married polytheist women?" So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work — those Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾. Allah replaced their worship of idols with the worship of Allah, replaced their fighting alongside polytheists with fighting alongside Muslims against polytheists, and replaced marriage to polytheist women with marriage to believing women.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾, said: "Shirk into faith, killing into restraint, and adultery into chastity."

⁕ I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ — this verse is Meccan, revealed in Mecca — ﴿And whoever does that﴾, meaning: shirk, killing, and adultery all together. When Allah revealed this verse, the polytheists of Mecca said: "Muhammad claims that whoever commits shirk, kills, and commits adultery will have the Fire, and has no good with Allah." So Allah revealed ﴿except one who repents﴾ from among the polytheists of Mecca, ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾, meaning: Allah will replace shirk, killing, and adultery with faith in Allah and entry into Islam, and this is the change in this world. Allah also revealed concerning this: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins﴾, meaning by it what was in shirk; Allah says to them: ﴿Turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him﴾, calling them to Islam. These two verses are Meccan, while the verse in Surat al-Nisāʾ: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ ... the verse, is Madani, revealed in Medina, and between it and the one revealed in al-Furqan are eight years, and it is ambiguous with no way out.

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, saying: Abu Ḥamza narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas was asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾, and he said:

*Budditna baʿda ḥarrihi kharīfā... wa baʿda ṭūli al-nafasi al-wajīfā*

[This is a verse by Labid al-ʿAmiri the poet. This version is obscure. I did not find it in the original of his diwan, but in the appendix to the diwan (Leiden edition p. 56), and its version there is like al-Suyuti's in al-Itqan. That version is better and clearer: *Baddalna baʿda al-nafash al-wajīfā... wa baʿda ṭūli al-ḥirrati al-ṣarīfā*. Labid describes a group of camels that used to graze at night for a long time, then were changed from that swift pace (wajīf), a kind of rapid march of camels and horses; one says: the camel and the horse hastened, wajfan and wajīfan. They were changed after long chewing the cud in their resting places (al-ṣarīf). "Ijtirāʾ" means that the ruminant brings back part of its food to chew it well, then swallows it again. "Ṣarīf" has several meanings, including milk at the time of milking and wine; here it means the sound of the camel's teeth when moved, which happens when it is exhausted and weary. Labid seems to say that their conditions changed after comfort into misery.]

⁕ Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation﴾. The polytheists said: "By Allah, these people with Muhammad were only with us." He said: So Allah revealed ﴿except one who repents and believes﴾. He said: "Repented from shirk," and "believes in the punishment of Allah and His Messenger," ﴿and does righteous work﴾: he said: "affirms," ﴿those Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾. He said: Allah changes their evil deeds that were in shirk into righteous deeds when they entered faith.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: those Allah changes their evil deeds in this world into good deeds for them on the Day of Resurrection.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr al-Basri related to me, saying: Quraysh ibn Anas Abu Anas narrated to us, saying: Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum related to me, from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: ﴿Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾: he said: "Their evil deeds will become good deeds for them on the Day of Resurrection."

⁕ al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafa narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ḥazim Abu Muʿawiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Maʿrur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I know the last of the people of the Fire to leave the Fire, and the last of the people of the Fire to enter Paradise. A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: 'Set aside his major sins and question him about his minor ones.' It will be said to him: 'You did such and such, and you did such and such.' He will say: 'O Lord, I did things that I do not see here.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molar teeth showed. It will be said to him: 'For you, in place of every evil deed, is a good deed.'"

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two interpretations is the view of one who interprets: "Allah will change their evil deeds," i.e., their deeds in shirk, into good deeds in Islam, by transferring them from what angers Allah to what pleases Him.

We said this is the more fitting interpretation of the verse because the evil deeds had already passed in their ugliness, and it is not possible to transform a thing that has passed with a certain attribute into a different state except by changing it from its previous attribute in another state. Thus, if this were done, the shirk of the disbeliever, which was shirk in its very essence, would have to become faith on the Day of Resurrection through Islam, and all his sins in their very essence would become obedience; and no person of sound reason would say that.

* *
His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾

The Exalted says: Allah is One who pardons the sins of whoever of His servants repents and returns to His obedience, and One who is merciful to him, not punishing him for his sins after he has repented from them.

* *
His saying: ﴿And whoever repents﴾

He says: whoever of the polytheists repents, believes in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and does righteous work﴾, meaning: acts upon what Allah commanded and obeys Him. Then Allah will do with him what He did with the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who repented, believed, and did righteous work before this verse was revealed: replacing his evil deeds in shirk with their goodness in Islam.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work, indeed he turns to Allah in repentance﴾: "This is for the polytheists who said, when ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ ... to His saying ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ was revealed, concerning the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'These were only with us.'" He said: "Whoever repents and does righteous work, for them is like what is for these ones: ﴿indeed he turns to Allah in repentance﴾ — repentance has not been forbidden to you."

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that will meet a penalty.﴾ (25:68) ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾ (25:69) ﴿Except for one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (25:70) ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work — indeed, he turns to Allah with a [sincere] return.﴾ (25:71)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Those who do not worship another god alongside Allah, so that they associate others in their worship of Him, but rather they devote worship sincerely to Him and single Him out for obedience. ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾ to be killed, ﴿except by right﴾, that is, either for disbelief in Allah after having embraced Islam, or for adultery after having been married (muhsan), or for killing a soul, in which case it is killed in retribution. ﴿And do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, that is, they do not commit what Allah has forbidden them to commit of intimacy with forbidden private parts. ﴿And whoever does that﴾ means: whoever commits these acts, invoking another god alongside Allah, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden without right, and committing adultery. ﴿Will meet a penalty﴾ means: he will meet a punishment and retribution from Allah's chastisement, as our Lord, may His praise be exalted, described it: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾

And among the meanings of ʾithām (penalty) is the saying of Bal'a' ibn Qays al-Kinani:

*"May Allah reward Ibn ʿUrwa, since he has become [one who commits] disobedience to parents, and disobedience to parents brings a penalty (ithām) for him."*

[[The verse is attributed to Bal'a' ibn Qays ibn Rabi'a ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yaʿmur, whose name is Ḥumayḍa, and he is of Kinana ibn Khuzayma. Bal'a' was the chief of the Banu Kinana in most of their wars and expeditions, and he conducted many raids against the Arabs, and he has reports concerning the wars of al-Fijar. He was a skilled poet who composed good poetry in every genre (see al-Mu'talif wa'l-Mukhtalif, p. 106, and Mu'jam al-Shu'ara' of al-Marzubani, p. 357). The verse was recited by the author of Lisan al-Arab (under "athama") and he attributed it to Shafiʿ al-Laythi. Abu ʿUbayda, in Majaz al-Qur'an, attributed it to Bal'a' ibn Qays al-Kinani, and the author [al-Tabari] took from him. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab: "Abu Ishaq said: the interpretation of ithām is recompense. Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani said: 'So-and-so met the ithām of that,' i.e., the recompense of that, for al-Khalil and Sibawayh went to the view that its meaning is: he will meet the recompense of the ithām. And the saying of Shafiʿ al-Laythi on this: 'May Allah reward Ibn ʿUrwa ... ... ... disobedience to parents, and it brings a penalty for him.'"]]

That is, the penalty for the act of disobeying parents, which is severing ties of kinship. Al-Layth said: "In the general sense of the exegesis, ithām means the penalty of sin." It has also been said regarding His words ﴿will meet a penalty﴾: it is a valley in Hell. Ibn Sayyida said: "The correct view in my opinion is that its meaning is: he will meet the punishment of ithām." End quote.

By ithām is meant: punishment.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a group of polytheists who wished to enter Islam, and who had committed these sins in their polytheism. They feared that Islam would not benefit them because of what had passed from them of such things, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, and Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed this verse, informing them that Allah accepts the repentance of whoever of them repents.

Those who said this:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Yaʿla ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that some people from among the polytheists had killed a great deal, so they came to Muhammad ﷺ and said: "What you call us to is indeed good; if only you would tell us that there is an expiation for what we have done!" So there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ up to His words: ﴿before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾ (39:53–55). Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said the same as the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, exactly.

- ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Muʿawiya, from Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ: "What are the major sins?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you; that you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you; and that you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to us from the Book of Allah: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash and Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from ʿAmr ibn Sharahbil, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you make a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." So there was revealed, confirming the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ ... the verse.

- Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar narrated to us, he said: ʿAli ibn Qadim narrated to us, he said: Asbat ibn Nasr al-Hamdani narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from Abu Maysara, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.

- ʿIsa ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿIsa al-Ramli narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle Yahya ibn ʿIsa narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, from Sufyan, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" Then he mentioned something similar.

- Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to me, he said: ʿAmir ibn Mudrik narrated to us, he said: al-Sarri — meaning Ibn Ismaʿil — narrated to us, he said: al-Shaʿbi narrated to us, from Masruq, who said: ʿAbd Allah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day, and I followed him. He sat on a raised piece of ground, and I sat beneath him, my face facing his knees. I seized the opportunity of his solitude and said: 'May my father and mother be ransom for you, O Messenger of Allah, which sins are greatest?' He said: 'That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you.' I said: 'Then what?' He said: 'That you kill your child out of fear that he will eat with you.' I said: 'Then what?' He said: 'That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour.' Then he recited this verse: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾ ... to the end of the verse."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, from Za'ida, from Mansur, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated to me — or I was told from Saʿid ibn Jubayr — that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abza ordered him to ask Ibn ʿAbbas about the two verses: the one in al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ ... to the end of the verse, and the verse in al-Furqan: ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ up to ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "If a man enters Islam, learns its laws and its commands, and then kills a believer intentionally, there is no repentance for him.
