We chose this reading just as one says "akhadhtu bil-khiṭām" and "akhadhtu al-khiṭām" (I took hold of the halter).

We have already explained the meaning of taḥiyyah and salām earlier, so there is no need to repeat it here.

* *

Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Abiding therein; how excellent it is as a dwelling place and a station﴾ (25:76) ﴿Say: "My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication. But you have denied, so the penalty will be inevitable."﴾ (25:77)

Allah, His remembrance be exalted, says: Those will be rewarded with the chamber for their patience, abiding in the chamber, meaning they will remain there, dwelling in it without end, and that chamber will be excellent as a place of settlement and a station for them, meaning: and a dwelling.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you﴾

Allah, the Majestic, says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to these people to whom I have sent you: What weight would my Lord give you, and what would my Lord do with you? It is said from this: "ʿabiʾtu bihi aʿbaʾu ʿabʾan" (I cared for him), and "ʿabaʾtu al-ṭīb aʿbauhu" (I prepared the perfume), when one prepares it, as the poet said:

*As if upon his chest and his two shoulders* ... *is a fragrant perfume that the bride has prepared through the night* [[The verse is by Abu Zubayd al-Ṭāʾī describing a lion (Lisan: ʿabaʾ). He said: ʿabaʾa al-ṭīb yaʿbauhu ʿabʾan: he made and mixed it; Abu Zubayd says describing a lion: "As if upon his chest..." the verse. It is also narrated as "bāta yukhabbiʾuhu." Al-Farrāʾ said in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān: His saying "mā yaʿbaʾu bikum rabbī" is a question, i.e., what would He do with you were it not for His calling you to Islam? Abu ʿUbaydah said in Majāz al-Qurʾān (p. 170): From it is His saying: "mā ʿabaʾtu bika shayʾan," i.e., I did not count you as anything.]]

He says: he prepares it and makes it, yaʿbauhu ʿabʾan and ʿabūʾan; from it is their saying: "ʿabbaʾtu al-jaysh" (with shaddah and without), so I prepare it (uʿabbiuhu), meaning I equip it. Al-ʿabʾ means a burden.

The interpreters of the Qurʾān have said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you﴾: He would do (yaṣnaʿu) for you were it not for your supplication.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you﴾: he said: "yaʿbaʾ" means "yafʿal" (does).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿were it not for your supplication﴾

It means: were it not for the worship of those among you who worship Him, and the obedience of those among you who obey Him.

The interpreters of the Qurʾān have said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abu Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication﴾: it means: were it not for your faith. Allah informed the disbelievers that He has no need of them, since He did not create them as believers; and if He had need of them, He would have made faith beloved to them as He made it beloved to the believers.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿were it not for your supplication﴾: he said: were it not for your calling upon Him that you worship Him and obey Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But you have denied﴾

Allah, His remembrance be exalted, says to the polytheists of Quraysh, the people of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: You have denied, O people, your Messenger who was sent to you, and you have opposed the command of your Lord, who commanded you to hold fast to it; had you held fast to it, My Lord would have cared for you. So your denial of the Messenger of your Lord and your opposition to the command of your Creator will be a constant punishment for you: killing by swords and a destruction that annihilates you, overtaking some of you after others, as Abu Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī said:

*So it overtook him with a constant (ʿādiyah lizām) ...* *as the basin (ḥawḍ) collapses, crumbling (laqīf)* [[The verse is by Abu Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī (Lisan: laqafa). He said: a ḥawḍ laqf and laqīf: it has collapsed at its base and widened; from it is Abu Dhuʾayb's verse: "Then you did not see except a ʿādiyah lizām." ... the verse. He said: it is also said: "al-mulaʾān" (full). The first is the correct one. He said: al-ʿādiyah: the people who run on their feet, i.e., they carried them constantly, as though they clung to it, not leaving what they were in. Ended. In (lazama) he said: al-lizām: the constant ones. Abu Dhuʾayb said: (the verse as in its narration in laqafa), then he explained it as he explained it there. He said: al-laqīf: the one collapsed at its base. Abu ʿUbaydah said in Majāz al-Qurʾān (Jāmiʿah manuscript no. 26059, p. 170): lizām: i.e., many, some following others; and in its margin: al-laqīf: the crumbled one, whose stones fell upon one another.]]

He means by lizām: the great [punishment] that follows one another; and by laqīf: the one whose stones fall and crumble. So Allah did that to them, fulfilled His promise to them, and killed them on the day of Badr at the hands of His friends, and joined some of them to others; that was the constant punishment.

The interpreters of the Qurʾān have said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, saying: a client of Shaqīq ibn Thawr informed me that he heard Salmān Abu ʿAbd Allāh say: I prayed behind Ibn al-Zubayr and heard him recite: "fa-qad kadhaba al-kāfirūn" (so the disbelievers have denied).

- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Adham al-Sadūsī narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Majīd, saying: I heard Muslim ibn ʿAmmār say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās recite this letter: "fa-qad kadhaba al-kāfirūn" ﴿fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman﴾.

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication; but you have denied, so the penalty will be inevitable﴾: he said: "the disbelievers, the enemies of Allah, have denied."

- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Dāwūd narrated to us, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "fa-sawfa yulqawna lizāman" on the day of Badr.

- Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to me, saying: Abu Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: five have passed: the smoke (al-dukhān), the lizām, the assault (al-baṭshah), the moon (al-qamar), and the Romans (al-Rūm).

- al-Ḥasan narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, regarding His saying ﴿fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman﴾: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: it is the killing on the day of Badr.

The interpreters of the Qurʾān have said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, saying: a client of Shaqīq ibn Thawr informed me that he heard Salmān Abu ʿAbd Allāh say: I prayed behind Ibn al-Zubayr and heard him recite: "fa-qad kadhaba al-kāfirūn" (so the disbelievers have denied).

- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Adham al-Sadūsī narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Majīd, saying: I heard Muslim ibn ʿAmmār say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās recite this letter: "fa-qad kadhaba al-kāfirūn" ﴿fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman﴾.

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication; but you have denied, so the penalty will be inevitable﴾: he said: "the disbelievers, the enemies of Allah, have denied."

- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Dāwūd narrated to us, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "fa-sawfa yulqawna lizāman" on the day of Badr.

- Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to me, saying: Abu Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: five have passed: the smoke (al-dukhān), the lizām, the assault (al-baṭshah), the moon (al-qamar), and the Romans (al-Rūm).

- al-Ḥasan narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, regarding His saying ﴿fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman﴾: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: it is the killing on the day of Badr.

- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: the lizām is the day of Badr.

- Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid: ﴿fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman﴾: he said: it is the day of Badr.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman﴾: he said: the day of Badr.

- al-Qāsim narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, similarly.

- He said: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyān narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Manṣūr, from Sufyān, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: al-lizām is the killing on the day of Badr.

- I was told by al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying ﴿fa-qad kadhabtum fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman﴾: the disbelievers denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and what he brought from Allah; so it will be a constant punishment, and it is the day of Badr.

- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: the lizām has passed; the lizām was the day of Badr, they captured seventy and killed seventy.

Others said: the meaning of lizām is: fighting.

Those who said that:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman": "fa-sawfa yakūnu qitālan" (then it will be fighting). Lizām: fighting.

Others said: lizām: death.

Those who said that:

- ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abu Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāman﴾: he said: death.

Some scholars of the speech of the Arabs said: the meaning of that is: then there will be a recompense that binds every doer to what he did of good or evil. We have already explained the correct view on this. There is another possibility for the accusative in lizām, other than what we have said, namely that the verb yakūn is passive, and then lizām is put in the accusative as predicate, as it is said: "idhā kāna ṭaʿnan baynahum wa qitālā" (when there was stabbing and fighting between them).

Some of those who had no knowledge of the sayings of the people of knowledge said regarding the interpretation of that: "Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication, what you call upon besides Him of gods and rivals." This is a view with no meaning to occupy oneself with, as it departs from the sayings of the people of knowledge among the interpreters.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Furqan, and all praise is due to Allah alone.
